items.title: Cardinals bid farewell to Nationals, Busch Stadium for 2026
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The visiting Washington Nationals will look to complete a three-game sweep of the St. Louis Cardinals on Sunday afternoon.
items.body:
The visiting Washington Nationals will look to complete a three-game sweep of the St. Louis Cardinals on Sunday afternoon.
It will be the final home game of the season for the Cardinals, who are 37-43 at Busch Stadium.
On Saturday, the Nationals scored four runs in the top of the 11th inning and held on for an 8-5 win. Washington (73-82) has won six of its past seven games, and a victory Sunday would give the team a .500 mark in September (8-8) despite a recent seven-game losing streak.
The Cardinals (75-80), meanwhile, have lost four games in a row. After Sunday's game, they will finish the season at Pittsburgh and Milwaukee.
Both St. Louis and Washington sit fourth in their respective divisions with seven games remaining, and both have been eliminated from postseason contention.
The Nationals will start right-hander Jake Irvin (2-9, 5.51 ERA) on Sunday, and the Cardinals will counter with rookie left-hander Quinn Mathews (2-3, 3.62).
Irvin has struggled since returning from the injured list in late July, going 0-5 with a 5.84 ERA in nine games (eight starts). Last time out, he followed an opener for the first time in his four-year career and gave up three runs on two hits and four walks over five innings against the Los Angeles Angels on Sept. 12. He struck out six and didn't figure into the decision of a 6-5 loss in 10 innings.
Irvin has allowed 16 first-inning runs in 19 starts this season.
Mathews will make his eighth major league start. Over his past four starts, he is 2-1 with a 1.93 ERA. In his most recent game, he allowed one run on four hits over 6 2/3 innings of a 2-1 win Monday against the San Francisco Giants. He struck out a career-high eight batters and walked two. He retired the first 10 batters he faced and did not allow a hit until the sixth.
"(Catcher Leo Bernal) kind of navigated the first three innings -- I think I shook one pitch in three innings, which is unbelievable, to be honest with you," Mathews said. "So a lot of credit to Bernal there, getting me through the first three when I wasn't as sharp as I would have liked to have been."
Saturday night, the Nationals won despite blowing their 40th and 41st save chances of the season, losing a 3-2 lead in the ninth and a 4-3 lead in the 10th.
Jose Tena had the big hit in the 11th, a two-run double, and the bullpen held on, with Will Dion getting the final out for his first major league save. Washington's Jorbit Vivas had four hits, and Daylen Lile smacked a two-run homer.
Jose Fermin and Ivan Herrera had three hits each for St. Louis.
The Cardinals pulled to 8-5 and loaded the bases with no outs in the bottom of the 11th, but Nationals relievers retired three hitters in a row -- two by strikeout -- to end the game.
For the game, St. Louis was called for a catcher's interference, committed two errors and left 13 men on base.
"They've done a really nice job of playing some pretty clean baseball," manager Oliver Marmol said of his team, "and even when we don't, you have the winning run up to the plate in extra innings. There's parts of that game that are highly frustrating."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Rangers look for length from Jacob deGrom in finale vs. Jays
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Texas Rangers have had to turn to their bullpen more often than they would have liked in the first two contests of their three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays in Arlington, Texas.
items.body:
The Texas Rangers have had to turn to their bullpen more often than they would have liked in the first two contests of their three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays in Arlington, Texas.
After pulling starter Kumar Rocker in the fifth inning of Friday's 7-1 win, Texas manager Skip Schumaker was forced to go to his bullpen with one out in the second on Saturday after starter Cal Quantrill exited the game with right lat tightness. Jordan Montgomery stepped in and held Toronto hitless over 3 2/3 innings in a 6-2 victory.
Schumaker hopes to give his relievers a breather when Jacob deGrom takes the mound in the finale against the Blue Jays on Sunday afternoon.
"That's what this team is all about right now," Schumaker said. "... Monty was fantastic. But again, these are team wins, and it's also because of what happened the day before, really covering us today."
The veteran deGrom (11-9, 3.79 ERA) has been strong at home this season. The right-hander has a 2.53 ERA with 111 strikeouts in 85 1/3 innings over 15 starts at Globe Life Field. He's coming off an outing in which he allowed just two runs on three hits in five innings against the Boston Red Sox on Sept. 15.
He has only made three starts against the Blue Jays in his career, going 1-1 with a 1.65 ERA.
The Rangers (78-77) are eyeing a third straight win and a seventh in eight games. Saturday's victory combined with the Houston Astros' loss to the Atlanta Braves, propelled Texas into sole possession of first place in the American League West.
"We're just here showing up every day to play and try and get in the playoffs," outfielder Wyatt Langford said. "To be in that position right now is great. But yeah, there are still a lot of games left. We need to keep it that way."
While the playoff picture is looking up for Texas, the hopes continue to fade for Toronto (76-79), which has dropped four of its past five. The loss dropped the Blue Jays to three games behind the final wild card in the AL, currently held by the Chicago White Sox, with seven games remaining in the season.
Toronto trailed 3-0 after two innings. The Blue Jays didn't get their first baserunner until Vladimir Guerrero Jr. walked in the fourth inning, and didn't get their first hit until the sixth.
But pitching struggles in the bottom of the sixth allowed the Rangers to tack on three more runs.
"It feels like the last couple games you're down early, and it makes it a little bit tougher to come back," manager John Schneider said. "You're looking for a big swing, a three-run homer or a base hit to score a couple to get back into it. I think falling behind early makes it a little bit tougher."
Spencer Miles (6-2, 2.65) will get the start in what is expected to be a bullpen game for Toronto on Sunday.
It'll be the second career appearance against Texas for the 26-year-old righty, who gave up just one hit in 2 2/3 innings of a relief appearance in a no-decision versus the Rangers on June 26.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Irán advierte de una nueva escalada de Estados Unidos y sus aliados
items.author: Jana Choukeir
items.creator: Jana Choukeir
items.summary: Irán advirtió el domingo contra cualquier nuevo ataque de gran envergadura de Estados Unidos y sus aliados, y dijo que disponía de información según la cual se estaba preparando una acción de este tipo, lo que aumentó la inquietud en una región ya sacudida por los ataques con drones y misiles contra Arabia Saudita .
items.body:
Irán advirtió el domingo contra cualquier nuevo ataque de gran envergadura de Estados Unidos y sus aliados, y dijo que disponía de información según la cual se estaba preparando una acción de este tipo, lo que aumentó la inquietud en una región ya sacudida por los ataques con drones y misiles contra Arabia Saudita .
El mando central militar de Irán dijo en medios de comunicación estatales que cualquier nuevo ataque desencadenaría una represalia sostenida contra las bases y los intereses estadounidenses, y que los aliados regionales de Washington serían considerados partes en el conflicto. No dio más detalles sobre la información de la que, dijo, disponía acerca de un inminente ataque estadounidense.
El Departamento de Estado de Estados Unidos emitió el sábado una alerta de seguridad en la que indicaba que existía la posibilidad de una escalada imprevista en Oriente Medio y que los estadounidenses debían redoblar la vigilancia y estar atentos a posibles cancelaciones de vuelos y cierres del espacio aéreo.
A punto de cumplirse siete meses de la guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irán, ninguna de las partes parece dispuesta a hacer concesiones importantes para poner fin a los combates y, con los mercados energéticos mundiales ya al límite, el conflicto sigue extendiéndose en la región.
El sábado, los hutíes de Yemen, respaldados por Irán, dijeron haber llevado a cabo ataques en la capital saudita, Riad, y contra una importante instalación petrolera en el puerto de Yanbu, en el mar Rojo.
Arabia Saudita no hizo comentarios sobre el incidente ni sobre las afirmaciones de los hutíes. La alerta del Departamento de Estado de Estados Unidos mencionaba las hostilidades de los hutíes contra Arabia Saudita, incluidos los aeropuertos civiles.
La reciente escalada de los hutíes ha obligado a Riad a enfrentarse a un doloroso dilema: continuar con los ataques aéreos contra el grupo para impedir que se apodere de más territorio yemení o dar un paso atrás con la esperanza de evitar ataques con drones contra infraestructuras críticas.
Los avances de los hutíes a lo largo de la costa significan que las fuerzas del grupo se sitúan ahora en el estrecho de Mandeb, lo que les facilita el control del tráfico marítimo entre el mar Rojo y Asia y les permite bloquear esta vía navegable crucial.
Dado que Irán ya ha bloqueado la mayor parte del tráfico marítimo en el estrecho de Ormuz, las exportaciones energéticas del golfo Pérsico, rico en petróleo, están ahora casi totalmente aisladas de los mercados mundiales, lo que aumenta la presión sobre los precios mundiales del petróleo.
Por su parte, el bloqueo estadounidense de los puertos iraníes impide a Irán vender su propio petróleo, lo que contribuye a los graves problemas de la economía de la República Islámica.
Irán reiteró el domingo que no reabriría el estrecho de Ormuz hasta que se cumplan los términos de un acuerdo de junio, tal y como los interpretaba.
El presidente del Parlamento iraní, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, dijo que Irán tendría que seguir luchando, además de negociando, para hacer retroceder a sus enemigos y consolidar cualquier avance logrado mediante la diplomacia.

items.title: Ronald Acuna Jr., Braves bid to clinch NL East in finale vs. Astros
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Atlanta Braves right fielder Ronald Acuna Jr. rode a torrid 20-game stretch into the middle contest Saturday of an interleague series against the Houston Astros, and he continued his stellar play.
items.body:
Atlanta Braves right fielder Ronald Acuna Jr. rode a torrid 20-game stretch into the middle contest Saturday of an interleague series against the Houston Astros, and he continued his stellar play.
Acuna finished 2-for-3 with two walks and a seventh-inning grand slam that sent the Braves toward a 6-3 victory. Atlanta (91-64) has a magic number of one to clinch the National League East title for the seventh time in nine seasons heading into Sunday's series finale in Houston.
Acuna was batting .363 with six homers and 16 RBIs over the previous 20 games, a stretch that started after he sat and watched the finale of a three-game series against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Aug. 27. Since then, he has more closely resembled the two-way threat who terrorized the NL before two separate season-ending knee injuries altered his stardom.
"And it's understandable, right?" Braves manager Walt Weiss said of Acuna methodically rounding into his superstar form. "When you have both knees reconstructed, it takes time to, not only physically, but mentally have the confidence in really letting it fly.
"I think we're seeing that now with Ronald again."
Left-hander Martin Perez (9-9, 3.07 ERA) will start the series finale for the Braves. Perez earned his first win in six starts -- and the 100th victory of his career -- in the Braves' 6-3 triumph over the Chicago Cubs on Tuesday, allowing three runs (two earned) on five hits and four walks with two strikeouts over six innings.
Perez was 0-3 with a 3.55 ERA in the five starts between wins, and he is 10-8 with a 3.72 ERA in 22 career appearances (21 starts) against the Astros.
Right-hander Hunter Brown (6-3, 3.43 ERA) is scheduled to start for the Astros (77-78) as they attempt to avert a three-game series sweep on Sunday.
Houston trails the Texas Rangers by one game atop the American League West and is two games behind the Chicago White Sox in the race for the AL's final wild-card spot.
Brown matched his season high with 10 strikeouts against the Kansas City Royals on Tuesday, allowing one run on two hits and three walks over five innings in a 4-2 win. He is 3-0 with a 2.86 ERA over his last five starts.
Brown is 1-1 with a 4.15 ERA across three career starts against the Braves. He recorded a 6-2 win over them on Sept. 13, 2025, allowing two runs on four hits and one walk with two strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings.
Left-hander Steven Okert, Houston's second-most consistent reliever behind closer Josh Hader, has spent the last two weeks on the injured list with a hamstring strain. His absence continues to be felt, as the Astros have struggled with high-leverage situations.
Right-hander reliever AJ Blubaugh allowed three runs on two hits and one walk while recording just one out in the seventh inning on Saturday. In seven appearances since Okert went on the IL, Blubaugh has surrendered nine runs on nine hits and five walks over six innings.
Right-hander reliever Bryan Abreu allowed a walk-off home run to the Rays' Junior Caminero on Sept. 11 and surrendered the grand slam to Acuna that flipped the game on Saturday. Previously reliable relievers Blubaugh and Abreu -- in tandem with Okert -- have labored lately.
"Those are our guys, and I trust them," Astros manager Joe Espada said. "And I'm going to continue to give them the ball."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Iran warns against new escalation by US and allies
items.author: Jana Choukeir
items.creator: Jana Choukeir
items.summary: Iran said it had information such a move was being prepared, adding to the anxiety in a region already on edge after drone and missile strikes on Saudi Arabia.
items.body:
Iran warned on Sunday against any big new attack by the United States and its allies, saying it had information such a move was being prepared, adding to the anxiety in a region already on edge after drone and missile strikes [USN:L1N45B003 TEXT:"on Saudi Arabia"].
Iran's military central command said on state media that any new attack would trigger sustained retaliation against US bases and interests, and that Washington's regional allies would be considered parties to the conflict. It did not elaborate on the information it said it had about a coming US attack.
The US State Department issued a security alert on Saturday saying there was potential for unforeseen escalation in the Middle East and Americans should exercise more vigilance and be aware of possible flight cancellations and airspace closures.
Nearly seven months into the US-Iran war , neither side has looked ready to make major concessions needed to end the fighting and with global energy markets already stretched, the conflict continues to spill over into other crises around the region.
On Saturday Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis, who made major advances along Yemen's Red Sea coast after the country's civil war reignited this month, said they had carried out strikes in the Saudi capital Riyadh and on a major oil facility in the kingdom's Red Sea port of Yanbu.
Reuters video showed a massive plume of black smoke billowing from the area of Riyadh's main international airport after booms were heard in the Saudi capital overnight.
Saudi Arabia did not comment on the incident or the Houthi claims, though a Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had foiled other attacks on the kingdom. The US State Department alert cited Houthi hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including civilian airports.
Recent escalation by the Houthis has forced Riyadh into a painful dilemma: continue airstrikes on the group to stop it seizing more Yemeni territory or step back in the hopes of averting drone strikes on critical infrastructure.
STRIKES ON SAUDI ARABIA The Houthi gains along the coast mean the group's forces now sit on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, giving them easier control over shipping travelling between the Red Sea and Asia and the ability to blockade the crucial waterway.
With Iran already having blockaded most shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, the oil-rich Gulf's energy exports are now almost entirely cut off from global markets, adding to pressure on global oil prices.
A US blockade of Iranian ports is meanwhile stopping Iran from selling its own oil, contributing to [USN:L1N44W081 TEXT:"major problems"] in the Islamic Republic's economy.
With the war inflicting painful damage on all sides, however, there is little sign of a return to the interim ceasefire agreement that was struck in June but that [USN:L6N43F0R2 TEXT:"fell apart"] in July amid disputes over its terms.
Iran reiterated on Sunday that it would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the terms of that June agreement, as it interpreted them, were met.
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said Iran would have to keep on fighting as well as negotiating, to push back its enemies and to consolidate any gains with diplomacy.

items.title: Un Israélien et un Palestinien abattus en Cisjordanie occupée
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Un Israélien a été abattu dimanche en Cisjordanie occupée par un tireur palestinien présumé, a rapporté la police, tandis que des soldats israéliens ont tué un automobiliste palestinien qui, selon l'armée, tentait de les renverser.
items.body:
Un Israélien a été abattu dimanche en Cisjordanie occupée par un tireur palestinien présumé, a rapporté la police, tandis que des soldats israéliens ont tué un automobiliste palestinien qui, selon l'armée, tentait de les renverser.
Selon l'armée et la police israéliennes, le tireur a ouvert le feu depuis son véhicule sur des Israéliens rassemblés à proximité de la colonie de Neve Tzuf, près de Ramallah.
Un homme grièvement blessé par balle a été déclaré mort à l'hôpital, a déclaré la police.
Le tireur a été localisé quelques heures plus tard dans un hôpital de Ramallah et arrêté, a-t-elle ajouté.
Peu après la fusillade, l'armée a annoncé avoir "éliminé" un automobiliste palestinien qui avait tenté de lancer sa voiture sur des soldats près de la colonie de Ganim, plus au nord en Cisjordanie. Aucun soldat n'a été blessé, a-t-elle ajouté.

items.title: El hermano de Diana compara trato que medios dan a Enrique y Meghan con el que sufrió la princesa
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El trato que los medios de comunicación han dispensado al príncipe Enrique y a su esposa Meghan es comparable al que sufrió su madre, Diana, dijo el hermano de la difunta princesa en una entrevista publicada el domingo, en la que advirtió de que era necesario aprender de aquella época.
items.body:
El trato que los medios de comunicación han dispensado al príncipe Enrique y a su esposa Meghan es comparable al que sufrió su madre, Diana, dijo el hermano de la difunta princesa en una entrevista publicada el domingo, en la que advirtió de que era necesario aprender de aquella época.
Diana falleció a los 36 años en un accidente de tráfico en París en 1997, mientras unos fotógrafos la perseguían en moto, lo que desencadenó una oleada de dolor y un debate sobre si los medios de comunicación tenían alguna responsabilidad en su muerte.
"Si te fijas en una noticia de un tabloide sobre Diana o sobre la pareja que mencionabas, Enrique y Meghan, ya sabes, pueden ser realmente, realmente desagradables", dijo a la BBC el hermano de Diana, el conde Charles Spencer.
"Y creo que la gente debería aprender del ejemplo de Diana".
"No estoy aquí para hablar en nombre de Enrique y Meghan, pero para cualquiera que esté siendo destrozado de esta manera a diario, debe de ser una influencia cancerosa en su vida", dijo.
Enrique, el hijo menor de Diana, y Meghan, mencionaron el impacto de lo que ellos denominaban "medios tóxicos" tenía en sus vidas antes de renunciar a sus obligaciones reales y mudarse a Estados Unidos en 2020.
También demandaron a gran parte de la prensa sensacionalista británica —con diversos grados de éxito— antes de regresar a Gran Bretaña en agosto.
Spencer ha acaparado los titulares de todo el mundo durante la última semana después de que su libro, «Swan Song: Diana, My Sister», se publicara por entregas en el Daily Mail, en el que acusaba a su exmarido, el ahora rey Carlos, de mostrarse «eufórico» en las horas posteriores a su muerte.
El palacio respondió afirmando que el rey «es consciente de que el dolor de la pérdida de un hermano puede nublar la razón, afectar al juicio y sesgar los recuerdos de formas que los demás no perciben, incluso muchos años después de dicha pérdida».
La publicación del libro y el regreso de Harry y Meghan a Gran Bretaña suponen otro reto para el rey, que sigue sometiéndose a tratamiento contra el cáncer.
La familia de Diana acusó a la familia real de mostrar una falta de apoyo o de atención hacia la difunta princesa antes de su muerte, una acusación que repitió Harry, quien actualmente se encuentra en gran medida distanciado del resto de la familia real.
items.raw_description: El trato que los medios de comunicación han dispensado al príncipe Enrique y a su esposa Meghan es comparable al que sufrió su madre, Diana, dijo el hermano de la difunta princesa en una entrevista publicada el domingo, en la que advirtió de que era necesario aprender de aquella época.

items.title: US, China trade teams set to huddle in New York to discuss AI, Iran
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: By Colum Murphy, Alicia Diaz and Yash Roy US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and China’s Vice Premier He Lifeng will lead talks on trade and other pressure points Sunday in New York ahead of next ...
items.body: By Colum Murphy, Alicia Diaz and Yash Roy US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and China’s Vice Premier He Lifeng will lead talks on trade and other pressure points Sunday in New York ahead of next week’s summit between the leaders of the world’s two biggest economies. The negotiators will lay the groundwork for a high-profile meeting between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sept. 24 in Washington. Bessent and He last met face-to-face near Seoul four months ago, just days before Trump visited Beijing in May.  Energy disruptions from the Iran war, the artificial intelligence boom, and trade and investment are likely to top the agenda as both sides work to maintain stability in a tariff truce that expires in November. Adding urgency for US officials to extend the deal are Nov. 3 midterm elections where inflation is a persistent voter concern. The US is “at a stage with China where efforts to try and transform this relationship and strengthen it are no longer top of list,” said Wendy Cutler, senior vice president at the Asia Society Policy Institute.  The objective is more about “trying to keep things stable, keep things from escalating and try to, in practical terms, keep the trade truce that was reached in Busan in place,” she said. “The Trump Administration will continue to pursue balanced trade with China by monitoring the implementation of recent commitments, optimizing trade in non-sensitive goods, and improving market access for American farmers, manufacturers, and workers,” he said in the statement late Friday. China’s Commerce Ministry on Saturday confirmed the talks would take place. An announcement of new US tariffs over allegations of trading partners’ excess manufacturing capacity has been delayed until after the meeting, according to people familiar with the matter.  “Both sides want to avoid another flare-up and relative stability in the relationship is likely to continue,” Nicole Gorton-Caratelli, Adam Farrar and Maeva Cousin of Bloomberg Economics wrote in a research note this week. “But as the US rebuilds its tariff wall, the risk of renewed escalation remains.” The US and China have been working to reduce levies on American energy and agricultural products, Bloomberg reported earlier, part of a broader initiative to ease barriers on $30 billion worth of products from each side under the Board of Trade mechanism launched earlier this year. Export Rebound Chinese exports to the US have rebounded this year, showing the limits of Trump’s tariffs but also reflecting a surge in demand for AI-related electronics produced by China. The New York talks are taking place ahead of the United Nations General Assembly meeting held in the city later next week.Bessent and He have held a series of discussion over the past 18 months mostly in a third country to portray a sense of neutrality. Whether the meeting in New York signals greater trust or merely convenience given the UN meeting, it also suggests the next round will be in China for the sake of reciprocity. Bloomberg reported earlier this week that Chinese officials were considering BYD Co. for a possible business delegation joining Xi at the summit — a potentially provocative move given Trump’s tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles.  Trump has suggested he might be willing to allow a Chinese car company to build in the US, if it did so with American workers.One Chinese official familiar with planning for the meeting said China’s top issue would be Taiwan, particularly a planned US weapons sale. Easier discussions will be held around tariffs and agricultural products like soybeans, while AI, autos, technology and e-commerce will feature on the agenda, said the official, who asked for anonymity to discuss private conversations. The official added that China would offer more permits for rare earths as a bargaining chip, without disclosing details on what Beijing would seek in return. Maintaining flows of Chinese rare-earth magnets was a priority for Trump when he agreed last year’s truce. Since then, China’s monthly exports of the critical industrial components have been running substantially below the levels that prevailed before Beijing imposed export controls in April 2025.  In recent weeks, AI has rapidly emerged as a new fault line between the US and China. ‘Fear-Mongering’ Washington has restricted China’s access to advanced chips and accused Chinese firms of developing their own domestic models by “distilling” capabilities from American tech. Beijing has pushed back on calls from US tech leaders to pace AI development in the interest of safety, with the country’s foreign ministry dismissing such moves as “fear-mongering” and state media denouncing them as “self-serving.” “As the number one and number two superpowers in AI by a lot, it behooves all of us to put up guardrails, to have close communication,” Bessent told reporters earlier this month. In a statement to Axios this week, the Treasury secretary said “we are open to discussions on avoiding shared risks and avoiding bifurcation of our two systems.” The US moves, Beijing says, are designed to contain its rise, and China refuses to let Washington take the lead on writing the rules for AI.  A more immediate threat to both economies is the energy shock, and the White House has stepped up pressure on Iran and its trading partners. China provides Tehran with an economic lifeline as the biggest buyer of Iranian oil.  Boosting Sanctions  Bessent’s Treasury Department is ratcheting up pressure on financial institutions as part of its effort to choke off trade and financial flows between Iran and rest of the world, fueling speculation that Chinese banks could be targeted.  Bessent said during testimony to the House Financial Services Committee earlier this week that he’s had “private discussions” with Chinese officials on the issue and hoped to make further progress during the upcoming talks this weekend. A US naval blockade has sharply curtailed crude oil flows to China, raising the prospect of refinery run cuts in the coming weeks across the teapot sector, which makes up one-third of national refining capacity. “China has an interest in reopening Hormuz, but limited leverage to force either side to change course,” said Jesse Marks, founder of Rihla Research & Advisory and former Middle East policy adviser in the US government. “The longer the Strait remains closed, the more US sanctions and the wider disruption to regional trade will begin to cut into China’s own economic interests in Iran.”

items.title: Resurgent Acosta beats Martin for maiden MotoGP win in Austria
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Pedro Acosta claimed the first MotoGP victory of his career in the Austrian Grand Prix on Sunday, bouncing back from his sprint-race crash to beat world championship leader Jorge Martin at KTM's home Red Bull Ring circuit.
items.body:
Pedro Acosta claimed the first MotoGP victory of his career in the Austrian Grand Prix on Sunday, bouncing back from his [USN:L1N45B02X TEXT:"sprint-race"] crash to beat world championship leader Jorge Martin at KTM's home Red Bull Ring circuit.
The 22-year-old Spaniard, who qualified third before crashing out while leading Saturday's sprint, seized the lead from [USN:L4N45B027 TEXT:"polesitter Martin"] on lap nine of the 28-lap race and never looked back.
Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi completed the podium, while Trackhouse rider Ai Ogura finished fourth.
It was an emotional moment for Acosta, nicknamed 'The Shark', who arrived in MotoGP with huge expectations after winning the Moto3 world title in 2021 and the Moto2 crown in 2023.
"The first one is always special," Acosta said. "Nice way to close a season like this with KTM in front of all Austrian fans. Super happy for them because they deserve it even more than me."
Acosta is set to leave KTM at the end of 2026 to join the factory Ducati team.
Martin, the 2024 MotoGP champion, got off to a brilliant start but was overtaken by teammate Bezzecchi for the lead at Turn One on lap two. The 28-year-old responded immediately, reclaiming top spot at Turn Three on the same lap.
However, Acosta's pace proved decisive and he passed Martin for the lead on lap nine before pulling away.
"I want to congratulate Pedro. He fought a lot during the last few years to get this victory. This feeling is amazing for him, so I'm really happy for him," Martin said of his fellow Spaniard.
"For myself, I think I did a great race. I was trying to manage the fuel. Then Pedro took me but I thought everything was under control. But step by step, he was stepping away. I tried to push a bit more but my rear tyre was completely destroyed. I did my best.
"This is what we have to do every weekend for the rest of the season, and the fight is on. So I am really looking forward to continuing like this."
Martin now has 306 points in the standings, a 12-point lead over compatriot and reigning MotoGP champion Marc Marquez ahead of next month's Japanese Grand Prix. Italian Bezzecchi is third with 264 points.
Marquez endured a frustrating weekend as Ducati lacked the outright pace of the Aprilias. The seven-time MotoGP champion qualified second but slipped back on the opening lap and eventually finished fifth.

items.title: Cubs eye potential playoff berth in finale vs. Reds
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Chicago Cubs could not ask for a better gift than a healthy Dansby Swanson for the playoffs.
items.body:
The Chicago Cubs could not ask for a better gift than a healthy Dansby Swanson for the playoffs.
Swanson came off the injured list on Friday after being sidelined for a month with a left oblique strain. On Saturday, he hit his 19th home run of the season to help the visiting Cubs record a 5-2 victory over the Cincinnati Reds.
Chicago (86-69) can clinch a playoff spot with a win on Sunday afternoon against the Reds and a loss by the Arizona Diamondbacks to the New York Yankees.
The Cubs are tied with the San Diego Padres (86-69) in the race for the top wild-card spot in the National League, one game ahead of the Philadelphia Phillies (85-70) and five games ahead of Arizona (81-74).
"This is like uncharted territory for me," Swanson said. "I'm just grateful for all the support from the team. Today was just a complete effort from everyone. I love when (reliever Daniel) Palencia is out there and believes no one can hit him. That is when he is best."
Palencia retired all six batters he faced in two innings on Saturday, striking out three.
"His two innings were his best outing of the year," Cubs manager Craig Counsell said of Palencia. "Through this last week, we have to find out about our bullpen, and this was a good step in that direction."
The bullpen took over for Matthew Boyd, who allowed two runs on two hits in five innings to pick up his first win since Aug. 9.
Four relievers allowed only two hits the rest of the way.
"If we want to be a team that plays for a long time, we need to get outs from the bullpen," Counsell said. "We have to figure out who is going to get it done."
The Cubs are expected to send left-hander David Peterson (8-8, 5.11 ERA) to the mound on Sunday. He is coming off a solid start in which he allowed one earned run on three hits in six innings of a 7-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves on Monday.
The 31-year-old is 1-2 with a 5.84 ERA in eight career appearances (seven starts) vs. Cincinnati (72-83), which has been eliminated from playoff contention and will counter with right-hander Rhett Lowder (6-11, 5.79 ERA) on Sunday.
Lowder's last win came on Aug. 28, a 10-8 decision over the Cubs. He yielded three runs on six hits in five innings to improve to 1-1 with a 3.60 ERA in four career meetings (three starts) vs. Chicago.
The 24-year-old is coming off a 4-0 loss to the Dodgers on Tuesday in a game in which he gave up three runs and five hits in five innings.
The Reds rallied to forge a 2-2 tie on Saturday with two runs in the fifth inning before the game slipped away.
"The only thing I would say is I'm jealous," Cincinnati manager Terry Francona said. "Me and Nap (bench coach Mike Napoli) were talking (Friday) night. We were looking at the scoreboard, like, man, that feeling of anxiety. I kind of miss that."
--Field Level Media

items.title: USA Trump transforme son projet d'arc de triomphe en "complexe militaire"
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré dimanche avoir accepté, à la demande de l'armée, de convertir son projet d'arc de triomphe à Washington en complexe militaire chargé d'abriter et déployer drones et munitions.
items.body:
Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré dimanche avoir accepté, à la demande de l'armée, de convertir son projet d'arc de triomphe à Washington en complexe militaire chargé d'abriter et déployer drones et munitions.
Le président américain a mentionné des préoccupations de sécurité nationale à l'appui de cette décision, sans mentionner de menaces spécifiques.
Donald Trump a déjà modifié son projet de salle de bal à la Maison blanche, contesté devant la justice, et le présente désormais comme un complexe militaire intégré nécessaire à la sécurité nationale.
L'autorité américaine de l'aviation civile a estimé vendredi que le projet d'un arc de triomphe d'une hauteur de 76 mètres près du cimetière national d'Arlington ne présentait pas de risque pour l'aviation civile à condition qu'il soit surmonté en permanence de spots éclairants. Des experts en aéronautique avaient émis des inquiétudes quant au choix du site, non loin de l'aéroport Ronald-Reagan.
Des anciens combattants ont également déposé un recours contre le projet en estimant qu'il abîmerait la perspective entre le Lincoln Memorial et le cimetière d'Arlington.
Depuis le début de son second mandat en janvier 2025, Donald Trump a entrepris de remodeler en profondeur la capitale fédérale avec la volonté d'y laisser son empreinte.
Outre la destruction de l'aile Est de la Maison blanche pour y construire sa salle de bal, le président américain a fait rénover le bassin réfléchissant du Lincoln Memorial, désormais recouvert d'algues, et menace de démolir le Kennedy Center, haut lieu culturel de la ville, depuis que la justice lui a refusé d'y accoler son nom.

items.title: Macron y Carney se reunirán en un archipiélago francés del Atlántico, en un gesto dirigido a Trump
items.author: John Irish
items.creator: John Irish
items.summary: El presidente Emmanuel Macron llegó el domingo al territorio francés de San Pedro y Miquelón para mantener conversaciones con el primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney, semanas después de que el presidente Donald Trump publicó una imagen en la que se veía a las islas cubiertas por la bandera estadounidense.
items.body:
El presidente Emmanuel Macron llegó el domingo al territorio francés de San Pedro y Miquelón para mantener conversaciones con el primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney, semanas después de que el presidente Donald Trump publicó una imagen en la que se veía a las islas cubiertas por la bandera estadounidense.
La visita de Macron al archipiélago situado frente a la costa atlántica de Canadá es la primera que realiza un presidente francés desde 2014 y coincide con un acercamiento de Canadá a la Unión Europea en un contexto de una guerra comercial cada vez más encarnizada con Estados Unidos.
San Pedro y Miquelón es el único territorio que le queda a Francia en Norteamérica, y las autoridades francesas dijeron que el viaje de Macron subrayaría la soberanía francesa y pondría de relieve los estrechos vínculos con Canadá.
"No hay duda (de que es francés)", dijo Macron tras aterrizar el sábado por la noche en este territorio de 5.800 habitantes.
"No vamos a afirmarlo todos los días porque la gente tenga ideas extrañas o diga cosas raras", dijo a periodistas en respuesta a una pregunta sobre el mapa de Trump.
LA VISITA TIENE UN PESO SIMBÓLICO Los diplomáticos señalaron que la visita de Macron, que se dirigía a la Asamblea General anual de las Naciones Unidas en la que se reúnen los líderes mundiales, tenía un peso simbólico tras la publicación de Trump en las redes sociales.
La imagen que compartió Trump mostraba la bandera de Estados Unidos extendida sobre Estados Unidos, Canadá, Groenlandia, Islandia, México, Centroamérica y el Caribe, y llevaba la leyenda "Estados Unidos de América". Incluía San Pedro y Miquelón y los territorios franceses del Caribe.
Francia no respondió públicamente a la publicación en ese momento.
Para Francia, San Pedro y Miquelón reviste una importancia estratégica debido a su ubicación a las puertas de Estados Unidos y del Ártico, explicó un responsable de la Presidencia francesa a los periodistas en una rueda de prensa previa a la visita.
El territorio también ocupa un lugar clave en la cooperación de Francia con Canadá, entre otros ámbitos, en materia de energía, uno de los temas centrales de la reunión del domingo entre Macron y Carney.

items.title: Federal Reserve rate hike reflects new world of sticky inflation and faster growth
items.author: The Associated Press
items.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has renewed his attacks on the Federal Reserve after it hiked its benchmark interest rate Wednesday, but the Fed matters less than broader economic trends when it comes to ...
items.body: WASHINGTON — U.S. President Donald Trump has renewed his attacks on the Federal Reserve after it hiked its benchmark interest rate Wednesday, but the Fed matters less than broader economic trends when it comes to longer-term borrowing costs, economists say. The economy is growing steadily despite being hit with repeated shocks — and may even be accelerating — while inflation remains stubbornly high. And big tech firms are borrowing huge amounts of cash to plow into data center construction while the federal government is still running large yearly budget deficits. All these trends point to higher interest rates regardless of what the Fed does, analysts say. As a result, the low interest-rate, low-inflation world that lasted for nearly 15 years after the Great Recession is over and a higher-priced, higher-rate world is taking its place. Mortgage rates fell into the three per cent range in the 2010s and even lower during COVID-19, but such deals are long gone. The average 30-year mortgage rate reached 6.95 per cent last week, the highest in more than a year and a half. Joe Brusuelas, chief economist at RSM, a tax consulting firm, said that a big reason for the change is a shift from the pre-pandemic economy in which consumer and business demand was weak, to the current economy in which healthy consumer and business spending is colliding with supply shocks and bottlenecks. In addition to higher oil and gas prices because of the Iran war, the AI buildout has struggled with an insufficient supply of computer chips, electronic equipment, and workers to put it all together. “We’ve undergone a structural transformation of the economy,” Brusuelas said. “The regime change in inflation and interest rates is the outcome.” Back to the future The shift, in many ways, returns the economy to where it was before the financial crisis in December 2007 that lasted through June 2009. But even after the downturn ended, consumer and business spending remained weak. Millions of Americans in the 2010s focused on paying down outsized mortgages and credit card debt instead. Businesses saw few investment opportunities, and many big tech firms such as Alphabet’s Google and Meta’s Facebook piled up cash. Now those companies are using those stockpiles to build out AI data centers, and are borrowing even more money to do so. And American consumers — despite surveys finding they are pessimistic about the economy — are still spending at a healthy pace. A recent report showing that retail sales picked up last month led economists at Bank of America to forecast growth will reach a healthy three per cent at an annual rate in the July-September quarter. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh highlighted the shift in a speech at the central bank’s annual conference in Jackson Hole, Wyoming last month. After 2008, “it was a widely held view that an excess of capital would sit on the sidelines for a long, long time, because there just wouldn’t be enough compelling investment opportunities,” Warsh said. “All the good stuff had been invented. So growth would be low and slow. “Well, times sure have changed,” he continued. “Ever-expanding pools of capital are pouring into AI-related infrastructure of all sorts.” The additional spending and investment has contributed to higher longer-term interest rates on government bonds that are competing for lenders. The yield on the 10-year Treasury bond topped 5% this year for the first time since 2023, even before the Fed raised its benchmark short-term rate Wednesday. At the same time, political polling and consumer sentiment surveys continue to find that many Americans are struggling to keep up with rising prices, and affordability remains a top concern heading into the midterm elections. Even as the economy expands, inflation has outpaced the annual growth in average wages for the past five months. Brusuelas said the U.S. economy’s expansion is “imbalanced” with growth “entirely dependent” on the AI buildout and strong spending by wealthier consumers, who have benefited from rising stock prices driven by hopes that AI will lift profits. Higher inflation leads to higher rates After the Fed lifted its rate to 3.9% Wednesday, Trump said on Truth Social that U.S. rates should be one per cent instead. Yet many of Trump’s policies have contributed to higher borrowing costs, in particular the Iran war that has driven up gas prices. When inflation persists, investors demand higher interest rates on longer-term Treasury bonds, such as the 10-year, which strongly influences mortgage rates. “The president can say he wants interest rates lower all he wants, and yet he continues to push the button on all the policies that raise rates,” said Elizabeth Pancotti, vice president of policy, advocacy and research at the progressive Groundwork Collaborative. Christopher Rugaber, The Associated Press

items.title: White Sox continue push toward playoffs in finale against Tigers
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Heading into the finale of a four-game set against the Detroit Tigers on Sunday afternoon, the host Chicago White Sox are desperate for a hero.
items.body:
Heading into the finale of a four-game set against the Detroit Tigers on Sunday afternoon, the host Chicago White Sox are desperate for a hero.
Miguel Vargas wants to fill that spot.
The All-Star slugged his 33rd home run of the season on Saturday to help Chicago (79-76) beat Detroit 3-1 and stay a game behind the Cleveland Guardians atop the American League Central. The White Sox hold a two-game lead over the Houston Astros in the race for the third and final AL wild-card berth.
"That's what I work for. That's why I wake up every day and work so hard for these types of moments," Vargas said. "And for me, this group has been pushing me every single day. I've never been thinking about my individual stats. I just want to go out there and do the best for my team and have some fun and always try hard."
Davis Martin (9-7, 3.96 ERA) will make his fourth appearance since being activated from the 15-day injured list (finger blister). The right-hander has a 1.13 ERA in three outings since his return, giving up just three runs (two earned), but he has only an 0-1 record to show for it.
Martin threw 5 1/3 innings of one-run, two-hit ball against Cleveland on Tuesday in a no-decision. He entered after Chris Murphy gave up three runs in two-thirds of an inning as the opener in Chicago's 7-6 loss.
Martin is 1-2 with a 3.49 ERA in seven career games (six starts) against the Tigers. The 29-year-old surrendered just one run on five hits across six innings in Detroit on June 21, striking out four and walking three in a no-decision. Chicago lost 5-4 in 10 innings.
On June 10, Martin had a 9-2 record and a 2.41 ERA after a 2-1 win over the Atlanta Braves. He has not won since, piling up five losses and nine no-decisions.
Meanwhile, Detroit (73-82) is nearing the mathematical end to a disappointing season. After consecutive playoff appearances, the Tigers will be eliminated from postseason contention with their next loss.
Detroit left 11 runners on base in the club's third loss in four games on Saturday.
"It feels good to have opportunities. It doesn't feel good when you miss out on them," Tigers manager A.J. Hinch said. "It's tough when you leave that many on, but you don't want to not have them on there and not have the chance."
As he makes his 20th start of the season for Detroit on Sunday, right-hander Troy Melton (8-4, 2.52 ERA) is looking to improve on what has been a forgettable September. After posting a 2.10 ERA in August, the 25-year-old has allowed 11 earned runs in 13 2/3 innings across his past three starts.
On Monday, Melton lasted just 2 2/3 innings against the Toronto Blue Jays. He gave up two runs on five hits while walking four and striking out three in a no-decision. He needed 76 pitches to record eight outs in a game the Tigers won 6-5.
In five career appearances (four starts) against the White Sox, Melton is 2-0 with a 1.48 ERA. He has faced them three times this year, going 1-0 with a 1.56 ERA, allowing three earned runs in 17 1/3 innings.
The Tigers are 1-2 in his starts against the White Sox.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Ucrania lanza el mayor ataque con drones contra Moscú, durante las elecciones en Rusia
items.author: Andrew Osborn, Vladimir Soldatkin
items.creator: Andrew Osborn, Vladimir Soldatkin
items.summary: Ucrania lanzó el domingo lo que el alcalde de Moscú calificó como el mayor ataque con drones hasta la fecha contra la capital rusa, mientras los rusos votaban en la última jornada de unas elecciones parlamentarias que el presidente Vladimir Putin ha presentado como una prueba del apoyo a la guerra.
items.body:
Ucrania lanzó el domingo lo que el alcalde de Moscú calificó como el mayor ataque con drones hasta la fecha contra la capital rusa, mientras los rusos votaban en la última jornada de unas elecciones parlamentarias que el presidente Vladimir Putin ha presentado como una prueba del apoyo a la guerra.
Los ataques con drones causaron la muerte de dos personas en la región de Moscú y otras dos en la parte de la región ucraniana de Jersón controlada por Rusia, entre ellas un funcionario electoral, según el alcalde de Moscú, Serguéi Sobianin, y las autoridades electorales. Ademas, resultó dañada una instalación de la refinería de petróleo de Moscú, que ya había sido objeto de bombardeos.
"Se ha repelido el mayor ataque de drones enemigos", dijo Sobianin en Telegram. "Este ataque sin precedentes fue claramente planeado con el objetivo de perturbar las elecciones. El enemigo no lo ha conseguido".
En las elecciones a la Duma Estatal, las primeras desde que Rusia inició su guerra a gran escala en Ucrania en febrero de 2022, se espera que el partido gobernante, Rusia Unida, conserve fácilmente su dominio en un sistema político que, según los críticos, no tolera la disidencia.
Es probable que el Kremlin presente el resultado como prueba del respaldo público a las políticas de Putin y a la guerra, que ya entra en su quinto año sin que haya indicios de que vaya a terminar pronto.
Las autoridades electorales han dicho que los tres días de votaciones se han desarrollado sin incidentes, a pesar de los ciberataques. A última hora de la mañana del domingo, la participación superaba el 45% tanto en las elecciones a la Duma como en las regionales, informó la presidenta de la Comisión Electoral Central, Ella Pamfilova.
A la mayoría de los candidatos contrarios a la guerra se les ha prohibido presentarse a las elecciones. Los que sí se presentaron, pertenecientes al partido liberal Yabloko, dijeron que temían por su libertad, después de que los tribunales condenaron a largas penas de cárcel a dos figuras destacadas del partido antes de las elecciones por sus comentarios sobre el conflicto.
Desacreditar al ejército o difundir lo que las autoridades consideran "noticias falsas" se castiga con largas penas de prisión.
En un pequeño acto de rebeldía, el líder de Yabloko, Nikolai Rybakov, anuló de forma ostensible su papeleta, escribiendo el nombre de su partido y el lema "Por la paz".
El Kremlin dice que la unidad nacional y cierta censura son necesarias durante lo que denomina su "operación militar especial" en Ucrania, que presenta el conflicto —el más mortífero de Europa desde la Segunda Guerra Mundial— como parte de una lucha existencial contra un Occidente hostil.

items.title: Luxembourg deploys additional detection assets following drone sightings
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Luxembourg's government said on Sunday that additional detection assets have been deployed to strengthen airspace monitoring, after Luxembourg Airport temporarily suspended services late on Friday due to the sighting of drones.
items.body:
Luxembourg's government said on Sunday that additional detection assets have been deployed to strengthen airspace monitoring, after Luxembourg Airport temporarily suspended services late on Friday due to the sighting of drones.
"To strengthen airspace monitoring and analysis capabilities, additional detection assets have been deployed, including resources provided by foreign partners," the government said in a statement.
"These supplementary systems have contributed to further consolidating airspace surveillance and contributed to a better assessment of the situation by the competent authorities," it added.
The government also said that on Saturday evening police "received several reports concerning the suspected presence of drones within national airspace" but that "following verifications, no situation required an operational intervention by the authorities".
Luxembourg's authorities launched an investigation after flight operations had been temporarily suspended on Friday evening following the visual sighting of "unidentified and unauthorized drones".
Prime Minister Luc Frieden told reporters on Saturday that his country had been "confronted with something new for Luxembourg, the presence of potentially bigger drones in the Luxembourg airspace".
"We have observed this over the past few days, which led to the precautionary measure last night," he said.
On Sunday, Luxembourg's government said its drone assessment cell is continuing work with partners to ensure monitoring of the situation.

items.title: Italy to ban veils in schools, limit foreign students per class, Meloni says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni played up her right-wing credentials at a youth event organized by her party.
items.body:
Italy is preparing to ban face coverings in schools and to cap the number of foreign students per class, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said on Sunday as she played up her right-wing credentials at a youth event organised by her party.
Italy is among the European countries most exposed to migrant arrivals because of its central Mediterranean location, making migration a hot-button issue and a major challenge for successive governments.
The integration of migrants, particularly those from Muslim-majority countries, remains contentious in Italian politics and society. Debates over religious symbols, cultural integration, citizenship rules and immigration policy frequently polarize public opinion.
"A measure will soon be presented to a Cabinet meeting to legally establish a maximum number of foreign students per class. It also requires parents of foreign students facing serious difficulties integrating into the school system to learn Italian and bans burqas and niqabs in schools," Meloni told an annual gathering of the youth wing of her Brothers of Italy party.
"If there is only one child in a class who doesn't understand Italian, that child will likely be able to learn the language and integrate quickly with the help of classmates and teachers. However, if the number of children who don't understand the language becomes large - or even the majority - that is no longer integration; it is neglect," she added.
Meloni did not specify what the maximum number of foreign students per class would be.
Students who are not Italian citizens account for 11.6% of those enrolled in Italian schools — nearly 12 in every 100 students — according to Fondazione ISMU, a research institution.
"You must go to school with your face uncovered, and in Italy no one, in the name of a real or supposed tradition, can decide that a young woman must hide herself, " Meloni said.

Tata Trusts challenges Chandrasekaran’s reappointment as Tata Sons chairman

Tata Trusts declares N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as Tata Sons chairman invalid, citing AoA violations and lack of affirmative director support.

New Delhi: The resolution to reappoint N Chandrasekaran as Chairman of Tata Sons was not validly passed at the company’s September 17 board meeting as the mandatory support of Tata Trusts’ nominee directors was not secured, Tata Trusts said on Sunday.

According to Tata Trusts, Tata Sons’ Articles of Association (AoA) require the affirmative support of a majority of directors nominated by Tata Trusts, which hold approximately 66 per cent of the company. With two Tata Trusts nominees on the board, both directors would have to support the resolution for the separate condition under the AoA to be met.

One of the two nominees voted against the resolution on September 17, meaning the required affirmative support was not available, the Trusts said.

Show Full Article

The Trusts further said the Chairman’s casting vote cannot be used to overcome the failure of this condition, as such a vote is available only in case of equality of votes at the overall board level and does not apply to the requirement concerning Tata Trusts’ nominee directors.

“There was no paralysis and there was no deadlock. The Board put a question, and the AoA answered it in the negative,” the Trusts said.

The Trusts also referred to the Supreme Court proceedings arising from the removal of former Tata Sons chairman Cyrus Mistry, arguing that Tata Sons had previously defended the affirmative voting rights of Trusts’ nominee directors under Articles 104B and 121.

The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal had held these rights to be oppressive, but the Supreme Court accepted Tata Sons’ position and set aside that finding, according to the release.

The Trusts said Tata Sons therefore could not now disregard protections that it had previously defended before the Supreme Court.

The Tata Trusts also rejected the argument that listing Tata Sons would be necessary to strengthen its corporate governance, pointing to existing provisions covering independent directors, audit and nomination committees, related-party transactions, retirement of directors by rotation and insider trading.

The Trusts said these governance standards had been adopted voluntarily by Tata Sons before the current issue arose. (ANI)

items.title: ウクライナがモスクワ攻撃、ロシア下院選最終日　与党が多数派維持へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Andrew Osborn　Vladimir Soldatkin

［モスクワ　２０日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Andrew Osborn　Vladimir Soldatkin

［モスクワ　２０日　ロイター］ - ロシアの首都モスクワのソビャニン市長は２０日、ウクライナによる過去最大規模のドローン（無人機）攻撃を撃退したと述べた。２０日はロシア下院選の投票最終日に当たる。

ソビャニン氏は通信アプリ「テレグラム」で「敵のドローンによる過去最大の攻撃を撃退した」とし、「この前例のない攻撃は明らかに選挙の妨害を目的に計画されたものだ。敵の試みは失敗した」と述べた。

同氏と選挙管理当局によると、ドローン攻撃によりモスクワ州で２人死亡。過去に標的となったモスクワの製油所施設も被害を受けた。またロシアが実効支配するウクライナ南部ヘルソン州で選挙管理委員を含む２人が死亡した。

＜下院選、与党が多数派維持へ＞

ロシアが２０２２年２月にウクライナへの本格侵攻を開始して以降で初となる今回の下院選は、反戦を掲げる候補者の大半の立候補が禁じられ、与党「統一ロシア」が難なく多数派を維持するとみられている。

選挙管理当局によると、１９日にサイバー攻撃が報告されたものの、３日間の投票はおおむね順調に進んだ。インタファクス通信が中央選挙管理委員会の情報として伝えたところによると、モスクワ時間の２０日午後早い段階で投票率は５０％を超えた。

暫定結果は２０日１８００ＧＭＴ（日本時間２１日午前３時）ごろに発表され、より詳細な結果は２１日に発表される見通し。

items.author: Stephen L. Carter

items.title: Palestinian gunman shoots dead Israeli in the West Bank, soldiers kill motorist
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: It was not clear whether the incidents on the eve of Yom Kippur were connected.
items.body:
Violence flared in the occupied West Bank on Sunday when a suspected Palestinian gunman shot dead an Israeli man, police said, and Israeli soldiers killed a Palestinian motorist who the military said was attempting to run them over.
The gunman opened fire from his vehicle at Israelis gathered at a spring near the settlement of Neve Tzuf, near Ramallah, according to the Israeli military and police.
Medics who arrived at the scene of the shooting said they found a man in a car suffering from critical gunshot wounds. He was pronounced dead at hospital, police said.
The gunman was located a few hours later at a hospital in Ramallah and arrested, police said.
Shortly after the shooting, the military said that its forces "eliminated" a Palestinian driver who had attempted a ramming attack on soldiers near the settlement of Ganim, further north in the West Bank. No soldiers were hurt, it said. Reuters was not able to immediately verify the soldiers' account.
It was not clear whether the fatal incidents, on the eve of the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur, were connected.
Following the incidents, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he had instructed security agencies to beef up their forces and carry out arrests and offensive activities in the area.
Palestinian militant group Hamas praised the shooting attack but did not claim responsibility for it.
Violence has escalated in the West Bank since Hamas' October 7, 2023, attack on Israel and the ensuing Israeli military offensive in Gaza . The West Bank violence has included a sharp rise in attacks by [USN:L6N44Y077 TEXT:"militant settlers"] on Palestinians, as well as sweeping Israeli military raids and Palestinian attacks on Israelis.

items.title: Trump to use Washington triumphal arch as military complex
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday the triumphal arch he plans to build near Arlington National Cemetery in Washington would double as a "military complex" housing drones and snipers, as well as storing large quantities of ammunition.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump said on Sunday the triumphal arch he plans to build near Arlington National Cemetery in Washington would double as a "military complex" housing drones and snipers, as well as storing large quantities of ammunition.
The president cited national security concerns for the move, echoing the rationale offered for the roughly $400 million ballroom complex being built on the site of the White House's former East Wing, which was demolished to make way for the project. He did not identify any specific threats.
The projects are part of Trump's ambitious effort to [USN:L6N41H110 TEXT:"reshape Washington"], including a push to add his name to the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. The plans have drawn criticism from preservationists and others who argue they could alter or diminish historic landmarks.
In a social media post, Trump said that at the "strong request" of the military he had agreed to turn the 250-foot (76-meter) arch "into a top grade Military Complex/Triumphal Arch, to house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large numbers of drones, plus Snipers, on both the roof and plaza areas, and additionally have and hold large quantities of sniper ammunition in storage."
The White House and the Department of Defense did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The Federal Aviation Administration said last week that the arch would [USN:L1N45A0PQ TEXT:"not pose a hazard"] to aircraft but would be required to have an "eternal flame" on top, clearing an aviation hurdle for the arch, which Trump proposed to mark the nation's 250th anniversary.
Aviation experts have raised safety concerns given its proximity to Reagan Washington National Airport while veterans have sued to block the arch, arguing it would destroy the historic sightline between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

items.title: Pirates' Brandon Lowe takes HR barrage into finale vs. Royals
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Pittsburgh Pirates will look to complete a three-game sweep of the visiting Kansas City Royals on Sunday afternoon behind Brandon Lowe, who has homered in four of his last five games.
items.body:
The Pittsburgh Pirates will look to complete a three-game sweep of the visiting Kansas City Royals on Sunday afternoon behind Brandon Lowe, who has homered in four of his last five games.
Lowe's two-run homer in the eighth inning on Saturday lifted Pittsburgh (78-77) to a 6-5 victory over Kansas City (67-88).
The win was the Pirates' 13th in their last 19 games.
Lowe's 33rd homer was the 96th hit by the club at home this season, breaking a franchise mark established in 1947. It also was Lowe's 19th homer at home, eclipsing Brian Giles' club mark, set in 2001.
"The best part of it is coming out with a win," Lowe said. "Records are cool, but a win is a whole lot better."
Even though the Pirates were eliminated from playoff contention on Friday, Lowe said the team has plenty of reasons to compete.
"It's never too late to get hot," he said. "It's a good time to get rolling and keep playing some good baseball ... The postseason thing won't happen, and that stinks. But we are still playing meaningful baseball when it comes to what the future of this organization can do. Winning is a whole lot better than losing."
Right-hander Lake Bachar (1-4, 3.50 ERA) will start for the Pirates on Sunday despite pitching one scoreless inning of relief on Saturday.
Bachar is 1-0 with a 4.50 ERA in two relief appearances vs. the Royals.
Kansas City will counter with right-hander Michael Wacha (9-9, 3.34 ERA), who will look to add to his career-high innings total.
Wacha, a 14-year veteran, set a career high for innings pitched on Sept. 8. He surpassed his previous mark of 181 1/3 innings, set in 2015 with the St. Louis Cardinals.
Royals manager Matt Quatraro praised Wacha -- who has 20 quality starts this season -- for his consistency.
"You can pencil him in for six (innings) every time out, if not more," Quatraro said. "... He has got really good stuff, he pitches down with the sinker, up with the four-seamer."
In his last start, Wacha took the loss, surrendering four runs on four hits with a walk and two strikeouts in a 4-2 road setback against the Houston Astros on Tuesday.
Wacha is 8-3 with a 3.59 ERA in 19 career appearances (17 starts) against the Pirates.
Carter Jensen launched his 25th home run of the season on Saturday, a solo shot in the third inning that established a rookie home run standard for the Royals. Bob Hamelin had held the record since 1994.
"He's a good player; I'm happy for him and his family," Quatraro said of Jensen. "That's an accomplishment that is going to be there for a long time, I imagine. The future is extremely bright for him."
--Field Level Media

items.title: European Commissioner discussed EU-Israel relationship, Gaza with Israeli minister
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The European Commissioner for the Mediterranean said on Sunday that she discussed the European Union's relationship with Israel, regional stability and Gaza recovery efforts with Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar.
items.body:
The European Commissioner for the Mediterranean said on Sunday that she discussed the European Union's relationship with Israel, regional stability and Gaza recovery efforts with Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar.
Dubravka Suica said in a post on X after the call that they discussed EU-Israel "relations and our shared interest in security and stability across the Middle East. This includes a reformed and functioning Palestinian Authority".
When it comes to Gaza, "I focused on the urgent need to advance early recovery," she said, adding that "our continued cooperation is key to delivering early recovery projects on the ground".
The commissioner announced in July that the EU and like-minded partners launched an initiative to help fund Gaza's early recovery focused on restoring essential social and economic services, rehabilitating critical infrastructure and strengthening governance.
The EU has criticised Israel's conduct in the war in Gaza while reaffirming Israel's right to defend itself. It has also criticised Israel's [USN:L8N42P0ZR TEXT:"expansion of Jewish settlements"] in the West Bank, widely viewed as illegal under international law and as an obstacle to Israeli-Palestinian peace and the establishment of a Palestinian state.
But the EU's 27 member states are divided, with some highly critical of Israel and others maintaining close ties.
Saar said in June that he was severing "all contact" with EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas over what he said were remarks attributed to her comparing Israel to apartheid-era South Africa.

items.title: Mets' Carson Benge eager to continue hit parade in matchup vs. Phillies
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The New York Mets spent the first half of their final homestand being reminded of what they were missing without Pete Alonso.
items.body:
The New York Mets spent the first half of their final homestand being reminded of what they were missing without Pete Alonso.
Carson Benge is closing the home schedule by providing the Mets a hint of what they'll have for the foreseeable future.
Benge and the Mets will look to end their home slate on a winning note on Sunday afternoon when they face the Philadelphia Phillies in the finale of a four-game series.
Mets right-hander Jonah Tong (2-1, 3.43 ERA) will oppose Phillies left-hander Cristopher Sanchez (17-6, 2.93).
Benge helped the Mets hurt the Phillies' chances of being in the top wild-card spot in the National League on Saturday, when the rookie outfielder homered among his three hits in a 10-3 victory.
The win was the second straight for the Mets (71-84) following a five-game losing streak that included a three-game sweep by Alonso and the Baltimore Orioles.
Alonso set the Mets' all-time record with 264 homers before signing with the Orioles as a free agent in December. He received standing ovations before every at-bat in Monday's 2-1 Baltimore win before he hit his 300th career homer in the ninth inning of Tuesday's 7-5 victory in 11 innings. The slugger went deep again in Wednesday's 7-1 rout.
But Benge nudged ahead of Alonso in one category in the Mets' record book Saturday, when his three hits gave him 156 this season, breaking the rookie high of 155 set by Alonso in 2019.
Benge's record-breaking performance is doubly impressive considering he opened the season with just 17 hits in his first 90 at-bats through April 30. He is batting .292 since May 1.
"I came in knowing I belonged," Benge said. "It was kind of rough there in the beginning, but (he was) sticking to my path and grinding out every day and now finally showing others that I finally belong here, too."
Benge's big day may have made the playoff path more difficult for the Phillies (85-70), who have lost 10 of their last 16 games to fall into the NL's third wild-card spot.
The Phillies are one game behind the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres, who earned wins later Saturday over the Cincinnati Reds and Miami Marlins, respectively. The final wild card will open the playoffs at the No. 3 seed, likely the NL East-leading Atlanta Braves, who are four games behind the Los Angeles Dodgers in the race for the second seed and final bye in the first round.
The Phillies have a four-game wild-card edge over the Arizona Diamondbacks, who beat the New York Yankees on Saturday night.
"I just don't think these guys are going to sit back and panic," Philadelphia interim manager Don Mattingly said. "We're in a better spot than a lot of teams, so I think we're positive on it. Honestly, we know what we're capable of."
Tong didn't factor into the decision in his most recent start last Monday, when he allowed an unearned run over six innings in the Mets' 2-1 loss to the Orioles. He has yet to face the Phillies in his career.
Sanchez took the defeat Tuesday after giving up five runs over 6 1/3 innings in Philadelphia's 6-3 loss to the Washington Nationals. He is 4-4 with a 3.97 ERA in 13 career games (10 starts) against the Mets.
--Field Level Media

Trump’s Greenland deal changes little. His bullying can change US-Denmark ties

As Donald Trump ended his confrontation over Greenland, European leaders were remembering the enormous risks taken as the Cold War began to descend on their borders.

Praveen Swami

20 September, 2026 05:05 pm IST

Facebook

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-
