items.title: MLB roundup: D-backs walk off Yankees on World Series anniversary night
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Pinch hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run, walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 on Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory over the Yankees.
items.body:
Pinch hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run, walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 on Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory over the Yankees.
Ildemaro Vargas walked to lead off the ninth off Michael Fulmer (0-1), reaching base after he appealed the 3-2 pitch that originally was called a strike. After a strikeout, Smith hit a 391-foot homer to right center for the D-backs' 46th comeback win of the season
Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells hit bases-empty homers for the Yankees, who had won four of five and eight of 10. Wells and Jose Caballero had two hits apiece.
Nolan Arenado had two hits and Jordan Lawlar added a two-run triple for the D-backs, who had lost three in a row and five of six.
The Yankees (89-65), who have clinched a playoff berth, fell five games behind Tampa Bay (94-60) in the American League East and remained 5 1/2 games ahead of Boston (84-71) for the top AL wild-card spot. The Yankees and Rays play a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader Tuesday.
White Sox 3, Tigers 1
Sean Burke hurled six quality innings and Miguel Vargas homered to help Chicago earn a victory over visiting Detroit.
Burke (10-7) allowed one run on five hits for Chicago, which remained a game behind American League Central-leading Cleveland. Sam Antonacci and Munetaka Murakami both drove in a run and Grant Taylor delivered a four-out save, his 10th overall this season.
Jackson Jobe (2-3) threw six innings of three-run, four-hit ball, striking out nine for Detroit, which remains barely alive in AL Central contention. The Tigers' wild-card elimination magic number is down to one. Kevin McGonigle drove in Detroit's lone run.
Mets 10, Phillies 3
Francisco Alvarez had two hits, including the go-ahead three-run homer in the fifth, as host New York routed skidding Philadelphia.
Carson Benge was 3-for-4 with a solo homer and two RBIs for the Mets. Brett Baty had two hits, including a run-scoring single, while Benge, Juan Soto and Bo Bichette each had RBI singles during a four-run eighth.
Alec Bohm had RBI singles in the fourth and fifth for the Phillies, who missed a chance to take over the top National League wild card, at least temporarily. The Cubs and Padres both won to remain tied atop the NL wild-card race.
Brewers 1, Orioles 0
Robert Gasser pitched seven shutout innings as the first of three Milwaukee pitchers in a victory against host Baltimore.
It marked the second shutout for Milwaukee pitchers in an eight-game stretch, needing only four strikeouts for the latest accomplishment. The Brewers scored on Gary Sanchez's second-inning groundout to knock in Joey Ortiz, who tripled with one out.
Baltimore has lost the first two games of the series following a three-game winning streak, further damaging its American League playoff hopes. Orioles starter Trevor Rogers (10-11) lasted eight innings, allowing one run and three hits.
Rangers 6, Blue Jays 2
Texas won for the sixth time in its past seven games, defeating Toronto in Arlington, Texas.
Rangers starting pitcher Cal Quantrill left the game after 1 1/3 innings with right lat tightness. Jordan Montgomery (1-0) replaced him and held Toronto hitless through 3 2/3 innings. Josh Jung gave Texas a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the first with a home run to right field.
Jose Soriano (12-8) gave up six runs (five earned) on four hits and struck out eight in five-plus innings for the Blue Jays, who dropped to three games behind the Chicago White Sox for the final wild-card berth in the American League.
Rays 2, Red Sox 1
Richie Palacios produced a two-out, walk-off single in the ninth inning as Tampa Bay edged Boston in St. Petersburg, Fla., to even their final home series of the regular season.
Against Garrett Whitlock (7-2), Palacios looped a 1-2 sinker into right to score Junior Caminero as the Rays hit their third walk-off winner during their nine-game homestand. Jonathan Aranda homered while Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson posted two hits apiece.
Caleb Durbin stroked two doubles and scored for the Red Sox, who lost for the first time in three games. Starting pitcher Brayan Bello went a season-best eight innings and allowed one run on five hits with a career high-tying 11 strikeouts.
Guardians 12, Athletics 6
Angel Martinez homered from both sides of the plate and drove in four runs in host Cleveland's win over the Athletics which helped maintain its one-game lead in the American League Central.
Martinez was also 4-for-5 with a double and three runs scored and Chase DeLauter also homered for the Guardians, who won their fourth straight. Slade Cecconi (5-7) got the win in relief with two scoreless innings after Tanner Bibee lasted 4 2/3 innings and surrendered six runs on 12 hits.
Donovan Walton hit a home run and was 3-for-3 with four RBIs for the Athletics, who have lost five in a row. Athletics starter and loser Jacob Lopez (6-5) was blitzed for 10 runs and 10 hits in 2 2/3 innings.
Nationals 8, Cardinals 5 (11 innings)
Jose Tena's two-run double keyed a four-run 11th inning and Washington beat the Cardinals in St. Louis.
Jorbit Vivas had four hits and Daylen Lile homered for Washington, which has won six of seven. Riley Cornelio (3-2) pitched 1 2/3 innings for the win.
At the top of the order, Jose Fermin and Ivan Herrera had three hits each for St. Louis, which has lost four straight.
Cubs 5, Reds 2
Michael Busch and Dansby Swanson hit solo home runs to lift visiting Chicago to a win over Cincinnati.
The win allowed the Cubs to pull a full game ahead of the Philadelphia Phillies for the top wild-card playoff spot in the National League. The Phillies lost 10-3 to the Mets earlier. The San Diego Padres also won to remain tied with the Cubs.
The teams will play the rubber game of the series Sunday. Cubs starter Matthew Boyd (9-5) gave up two hits and two runs (one earned) in five innings. Reds starter Nick Lodolo (3-6) gave up seven hits and three runs in seven innings.
Pirates 6, Royals 5
Brandon Lowe launched a go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth inning to power Pittsburgh to a victory over visiting Kansas City.
Ronny Simon and Jake Mangum each hit two-run homers, while Oneil Cruz, Rafael Flores Jr. and Lowe each had two hits for the Pirates. Right-hander Luke Weaver (3-1) threw a scoreless eighth with one strikeout, and left-hander Mason Montgomery earned his 15th save of the season after working around a walk with one strikeout in a scoreless ninth.
Nick Loftin had four hits, while Bobby Witt Jr. went 3-for-5 with two runs and extended his on-base streak to 17 games for the Royals. Carter Jensen hit a solo homer, while Jac Caglianone and Vinnie Pasquantino each had two hits for Kansas City.
Braves 6, Astros 3
Ronald Acuna Jr. hit a grand slam, Grant Holmes produced a quality start and Atlanta lowered its magic number to one to clinch the National League East by defeating host Houston.
The Braves secured this three-game interleague series and set the table to win the NL East for the seventh time in nine seasons with a victory in the series finale on Sunday. Holmes (10-5) allowed two runs on eight hits over six innings. Closer Raisel Iglesias notched his 34th save for Atlanta.
The Astros dropped a game behind the Rangers in the AL West after Texas beat Toronto. Astros reliever AJ Blubaugh (5-3) loaded the bases and was replaced by Bryan Abreu, who gave up Acuna's homer in the seventh inning for a 5-2 Braves lead.
Rockies 5, Mariners 3
Cole Carrigg delivered a go-ahead two-run single in a four-run seventh inning as Colorado edged Seattle in Denver.
Juan Mejia (4-6) pitched two scoreless innings and Brennan Bernardino got the final three outs for his second save for Colorado. Jake McCarthy and TJ Rumfield each produced an RBI.
Cal Raleigh and Randy Arozarena homered and Julio Rodriguez and Michael Arroyo had two hits each for Seattle, which is on the brink of elimination in the AL wild-card race.
Padres 6, Marlins 5 (10 innings)
Rookie Ethan Salas stroked an RBI single in the bottom of the 10th inning and San Diego edged visiting Miami.
Salas' hit scored Jake Cronenworth, who started the inning as the automatic runner at second base and advanced to third on a wild pitch by Josh Ekness (2-4). David Morgan (4-1) stranded runners at first and second in the top of the 10th to earn the win, San Diego's 12th in 13 games.
The Padres tied the Chicago Cubs for the top wild-card spot in the National League at 86-69. Miami forced extra innings when pinch hitter Griffin Conine pulled a 102 mph fastball from closer Mason Miller for a game-tying homer with one out in the ninth.
Dodgers 10, Giants 4
Mookie Betts tied a season high with four hits, Tommy Edman delivered a go-ahead two-run single and Los Angeles stayed within two games of the best record in the National League with a victory over visiting San Francisco.
Betts has 10 hits over his past three games, including seven in the past two while operating out of the leadoff spot in place of an injured Shohei Ohtani. Will Smith homered as the Dodgers won for the fifth time in six games and improved to 13-3 since Sept. 3. Tarik Skubal (11-7) gave up four runs on eight hits over five innings.
Victor Bericoto hit a home run among his two hits for the Giants while Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings in his fourth career appearance and second start.
Angels 6, Twins 5 (11 innings)
Christian Moore singled in automatic runner Zach Neto with a bases-loaded comebacker off pitcher Taylor Rogers' leg with two outs in the bottom of the 11th inning as Los Angeles edged Minnesota in Anaheim, Calif.
Moore drilled a first-pitch sweeper that caromed off the leg of Rogers (6-4) and back toward the third base line as Neto sprinted home. Tayler Saucedo (1-1) struck out two during a scoreless inning of relief for the Angels, who tied it at 5-5 in the bottom of the ninth on Vaughn Grissom's homer.
Ryan Kreidler hit a home run, Victor Caratini went 2-for-5 with two RBIs, Walker Jenkins had two hits and a run and Josh Bell and Royce Lewis each had two hits for the Twins.
--Field Level Media

items.title: South Korea miss practice before men's basketball final due to bus no-show
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The South Korean men's basketball team missed a light practice session on Sunday, hours before they take on hosts Japan in the Asian Games final, after their shuttle bus did not show up, news agency Yonhap reported.
items.body:
The South Korean men's basketball team missed a light practice session on Sunday, hours before they take on hosts Japan in the Asian Games final, after their shuttle bus did not show up, news agency Yonhap reported.
The bus, scheduled to arrive at the team hotel in Nagoya at 10 a.m., failed to arrive, team officials told the South Korean news agency, saying they had received no explanation.
South Korea, aiming to win their first men's basketball gold in the Asian Games since 2014, were set for a shoot-around session at a practice gym in the morning before the final, which starts at 7:40 p.m. (1040 GMT) at the Aichi International Arena.
The Korean Sport & Olympic Committee told Yonhap it planned to lodge a complaint with the Asian Games organising committee and the Olympic Council of Asia.
Asked for comment, the organisers declined to comment on the incident but told Reuters in an email: "We are working to arrange appropriate transportation services for all athletes, coaches, and event staff to ensure that the competition is not affected."
Multiple organising missteps have plagued the Aichi-Nagoya Games, including accommodation issues and transport mishaps.
South Korea's soccer team faced delays and were driven to the wrong stadium, while the country's hockey players were left bemused when the anthem of rival North Korea was played by mistake during the pre-match ceremony.

items.title: Saudi, Gulf stocks fall after Houthis claim Riyadh attacks
items.author: Ateeq Shariff
items.creator: Ateeq Shariff
items.summary: Saudi Arabia's stock market fell on Sunday, a day after Yemen's Houthis said they struck sensitive targets in Riyadh with missiles and drones, with the subdued sentiment seeing all the Gulf bourses close lower.
items.body:
Saudi Arabia's stock market fell on Sunday, a day after Yemen's Houthis said they [USN:L1N45B003 TEXT:"struck "sensitive" targets in Riyadh"] with missiles and drones, with the subdued sentiment seeing all the Gulf bourses close lower.
Flames and thick smoke were seen near the Saudi capital's main airport on Saturday after authorities issued overnight alerts warning of potential danger around Riyadh.
The confrontation has become another front in the broader conflict that followed US and Israeli strikes on Iran in late February. President Donald Trump has reportedly rejected Saudi requests for direct US military intervention against the Houthis.
Saudi Arabia's benchmark index (.TASI) pared early losses to close 0.3% lower, hit by a 2.8% drop in ACWA Power Co (2082.SE) .
Attention is turning to US President Donald Trump's meeting with Gulf leaders this week, where any meaningful de-escalation signals could support investor confidence, said Daniel Takieddine, co-founder and CEO of Sky Links Capital Group.
Oil major Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) closed 1.3% higher after falling in early trade.
China has [USN:L8N4590LF TEXT:"privately urged Tehran"] to help restrain the Iran-aligned Houthis, following a Saudi appeal to Beijing, according to three Iranian sources familiar with the discussions.
In Qatar, the main index (.QSI) retreated 1.1%, pressured by a 4.1% drop in petrochemical producer Industries Qatar (IQCD.QA) .
Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index (.EGX30) eased 0.2%.
Saudi Arabia (.TASI) fell 0.3% to 10,750 Qatar (.QSI) declined 1.1% to 9,550 Egypt (.EGX30) lost 0.2% to 55,371 Bahrain (.BAX) was down 0.2% to 1,920 Oman (.MSX30) eased 0.3% to 7,580 Kuwait (.BKP) dropped 0.7% to 9,182

items.title: 円相場に一段安リスク、日銀の利上げ姿勢に失望感－連休で流動性低下
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 円相場は今後1週間にわたり、値動きが荒くなり、一段安となる可能性がある。日本がシルバーウィークの大型連休に入り取引の流動性が低下するほか、日本銀行が今後の利上げペースについてより明確な指針を示さなかったことに投資家が失望しているためだ。

取引は21日に再開する。円は18日、対ドルで一時1.3%下落した。同日、日銀が利上げを決めた際には政策委員2人が反対した。その後、日銀が市場参加者に為替水準を照会するレートチェックを実施したと報じられた。円相場を押し上げるための円買い介入に向けた前段階となる可能性があるが、円の下げ幅を縮小するにとどまった。円は156円88銭で取引を終え、週間では2%以上下落した。

キャピタル・エコノミクスのシニア市場エコノミスト、ジェームズ・ライリー氏はリポートで、「最近は円が勢いをつけて日銀会合を迎えても、たいていの場合、日銀がその流れを完全に止めてしまっている」と指摘。「円が対ドルで大きく持ち直すかどうかは、米国側の動きにかかっていると言ってよさそうだ」と記した。

報道されたレートチェックは、円の一段安を食い止めるため当局が再び市場介入に踏み切るリスクを浮き彫りにしている。介入があれば相場が急変し、トレーダーが損失を被る可能性がある。日本では23日まで祝日が続くため流動性の低下が見込まれ、当局が介入した場合、その効果を増幅させる好機となる。4月下旬から5月上旬のゴールデンウイーク前後にも同様の機会があり、円が160円を超えて下落した後、日本は市場介入に踏み切った。

直近の円買い介入は7月下旬に始まり、米国も日本とともに市場介入に加わった。これを受け、円は6%以上上昇した。円高は9月8日の152円89銭でピークを付けたが、先週までは円の先行きに比較的楽観的な投資家もいた。

HSBCホールディングスのアジア為替調査責任者、ジョーイ・チュー氏はリポートで、「ドル・円相場が転換点を迎えつつあるのかを見極めようとしていた」とした上で、「最近のイベント（協調介入、わずか3カ月後の2回目の利上げ）は、ドル・円相場を安定させるにとどまり、下落基調に転じさせるものではないと現在はみている」と述べた。

items.title: 台風25号が関東に接近見込み､大雨に警戒呼びかけ-首都圏在来線運休も
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 大型で強い台風25号は21日から22日にかけて関東甲信地方に接近する見込みだ。気象庁は大雨や突風などに警戒を呼び掛けており、既に鉄道など交通網の一部に影響が出ている。

気象庁の20日午前11時時点の発表によると、台風25号は20日午前9時時点で日本の南に位置し、1時間におよそ10キロの速さで北西へ進んでいた。中心気圧は970ヘクトパスカル、最大瞬間風速は50メートルで、21日昼前から夜遅くにかけて関東甲信地方に近づく見通し。

JR東日本は21日に内房線や青梅線などの一部区間で運転を取りやめるほか、山手線など他の主な首都圏の在来線でも22日早朝にかけて遅れや運休が発生する場合があるとしている。全日本空輸（ANA）は21日まで八丈島空港を発着する全ての便を欠航するほか、成田空港や羽田空港などを発着する便でも影響が懸念されるという。

大型イベントにも影響が出ており、ゲームの見本市「東京ゲームショウ」や野外音楽フェス「ロック・イン・ジャパン・フェスティバル」は21日の開催中止が発表された。

items.title: Francisco Alvarez's blast ignites Mets rout of Phillies
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Francisco Alvarez had two hits Saturday, including the go-ahead three-run homer in the fifth, as the host New York Mets routed the skidding Philadelphia Phillies 10-3.
items.body:
Francisco Alvarez had two hits Saturday, including the go-ahead three-run homer in the fifth, as the host New York Mets routed the skidding Philadelphia Phillies 10-3.
Carson Benge was 3-for-4 with a solo homer and two RBIs for the Mets (71-84), who have won the middle two games of the four-game series. Brett Baty had two hits, including a run-scoring single, while Benge, Juan Soto and Bo Bichette each had RBI singles during a four-run eighth.
Ronny Mauricio and Francisco Lindor worked bases-loaded walks.
Jefry Yan (2-1), the first of five Mets relievers, earned the win by allowing two hits over 1 1/3 innings. Cionel Perez, Jonathan Pintaro, Dedniel Nunez and Tobias Myers combined to blank the Phillies on one hit over the final three innings.
Mets starter Christian Scott allowed three runs on six hits and one walk while striking out seven over 4 2/3 innings.
Alec Bohm had RBI singles in the fourth and fifth for the Phillies (85-70), who missed a chance to take over the top National League wild card, at least temporarily. The Chicago Cubs (86-69) and San Diego Padres (86-69) both won to remain tied atop the NL wild-card race.
Bryce Harper had a double and sacrifice fly while Trea Turner and Luis Arraez added two hits apiece for the Phillies, who fell to 7-10 in September.
Andrew Painter (3-10) took the loss after surrendering four runs on four hits and one walk while striking out six over 5 1/3 innings.
Benge homered leading off the second. Bohm tied the score in the fourth before the Phillies chased Scott in the fifth when Harper lofted a tie-breaking sacrifice fly before Bohm's RBI single to left off Yan.
The Mets took the lead in a 10-pitch span against Painter leading off the bottom of the inning. Marcus Semien drew a four-pitch walk and Baty singled before Alvarez hit a 387-foot opposite field homer to right.
Mauricio drew a bases-loaded walk in the sixth, as did Lindor in the eighth before the consecutive RBI singles by Soto, Bichette and Benge.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Weight-cut heartbreak returns to haunt India on day of mixed MMA fortunes
items.author: Amlan Chakraborty
items.creator: Amlan Chakraborty
items.summary: Two years after wrestler Vinesh Phogat famously missed out on Olympic glory by just 100 grams, India suffered another weight-cut heartbreak on Sunday when mixed martial arts fighter Varun Sanyal was declared medically unfit ahead of his men's traditional 77kg quarter-final bout.
items.body:
Two years after wrestler Vinesh Phogat famously missed out on Olympic glory by just 100 grams, India suffered another weight-cut heartbreak on Sunday when mixed martial arts fighter Varun Sanyal was declared medically unfit ahead of his men's traditional 77kg quarter-final bout.
While Phogat was disqualified for being [USN:L4N3JU15K TEXT:"100 grams overweight"] ahead of her gold-medal bout in Paris despite cutting her hair and wearing a smaller singlet, Sanyal's campaign ended before it had even begun after he grew dizzy during a sauna session that most fighters undergo as part of their weight-cutting process ahead of a bout.
"Varun Sanyal suffered from generalised cramps and bodyache while in the sauna last evening in his cruise accommodation," the Indian Olympic Association said in a statement.
"He underwent a medical examination and precautionary blood tests, which were normal. Despite rest, the following morning, he felt not fully fit to participate in a combat sport. After consultation with his coach, he withdrew on medical grounds."
Fellow MMA fighter Suchika Tariyal restored smiles in the Indian camp later in the day, guaranteeing herself at least a bronze medal in a new highlight for the 36-year-old's remarkable multi-discipline career.
A 2024 world champion in jiu-jitsu, a Commonwealth Games judoka four years ago, and a kurash competitor at the previous Asian Games, Tariyal is now competing in mixed martial arts as the sport makes its Asian Games debut in Aichi-Nagoya.
The Indian dominated Mongolia's Altanchimeg Baigalmaa in the women's traditional 60kg quarter-final, thoroughly justifying her latest switch across combat sports.
"She's 36 years old and she is doing this. She is an inspiration," her coach Nikhil Kunder said.
"She motivates me to train harder every time we get on the mat and when she trains at my gym, she motivates all my young fighters."
Tariyal, who serves in India's central armed police forces, said the triumph followed a long series of hardships and would have been impossible without the unwavering support of her husband.
"Financially it has been hard. I had to take unpaid leave. I am not getting a salary now," she said.
"My husband had to take a loan to allow me to travel to these qualifying events and even to train. He is my greatest support.
"A lot of times after marriage, husbands in India do not allow their wives to pursue their sporting careers ... I have come this far because of my husband's support."
The colour of her medal will depend on how Tariyal fares in Monday’s semi-final, with a potential final to follow a day later.

items.title: Davis Cup roundup: Czech Republic ousts U.S. in second round
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The host Czech Republic rallied from a 2-1 deficit and captured both reverse singles matches over the United States to win 3-2 in Round 2 of Davis Cup qualifying play on Saturday in Prague.
items.body:
The host Czech Republic rallied from a 2-1 deficit and captured both reverse singles matches over the United States to win 3-2 in Round 2 of Davis Cup qualifying play on Saturday in Prague.
The Czech Republic will advance to the quarterfinals, while the United States has been eliminated.
Davis Cup series are being contested worldwide this weekend to determine the seven teams that will join defending champion Italy in the final stage at Bologna, Italy, from Nov. 24-29.
The United States took a 2-1 lead when the doubles duo of Christian Harrison and Austin Krajicek pulled out a third-set tiebreaker to defeat Adam Pavlasek and Patrik Rikl 5-7, 6-3, 7-6 (8).
U.S. Open finalist Ben Shelton, who dropped his Friday singles match to Jiri Lehecka, captured the first set over Jakub Mensik. But the world No. 15 rallied to defeat Shelton 5-7, 6-4, 6-3 to knot the match at 2-2.
American Learner Tien, who got his side off to a 1-0 lead on Friday, took on Lehecka in the deciding match. In a match that featured six breaks of serve, Lehecka earned four of the six to defeat Tien 6-3, 7-5 and oust the U.S. squad.
Austria 3, Belgium 1
Jurji Rodionov, ranked No. 142 in the world, upset No. 38 Zizou Bergs, 7-6 (6), 6-3 and propelled Austria over Belgium in Vienna.
The Austrian doubles team of Lucas Mielder and Neil Oberleitner broke a 1-1 tie by edging Sander Gille and Joran Vliegan, 7-6 (5), 7-5.
That set up Rodionov, who had routed Gauthier Onclin, 6-4, 6-1, on Friday. In the first set, he had two break points at 6-5 over Bergs, but the Belgian held to force a tie-breaker. Bergs had a set point at 6-5 in the breaker, but the 27-year old Rodionov won three straight points to capture the set.
Rodionov broke Bergs in all four of his service games in the second set.
South Korea 3, India 1
After India won the doubles, Soonwoo Kwon won his second singles match to lead his squad to victory in Seoul.
Kwon easily got past India's Sumit Nagal, 6-1, 6-2. The 28-year-old, who did not play internationally from January 2025 to June 2026 due to military service, led off on Friday with a 3-6, 6-3, 6-4 victory over Dhakshineswar Suresh.
India's doubles duo of N Sriram Balaji and Suresh forced a fourth match with a 6-3, 3-6, 6-3 triumph over NamJi-sung Nam and Park Ui-sung.
Canada 3, France 1
World No. 5 Felix Auger-Aliassime edged Arthur Rinderknech in three sets to propel Canada to an upset victory over France in Quebec City.
Auger-Aliassime won both his matches in three sets. On Friday, he followed up a stunning win by unheralded countryman Liam Draxl, getting past Quentin Halys, 7-6 (5), 4-6, 6-3.
After France trimmed the deficit to 2-1, the lanky Auger-Aliassime dropped the first set to Rinderknech, but rallied to win, 4-6, 7-6 (5), 6-4. The Canadian ripped 17 aces and won 67 of 86 points (77.9%) of his service points.
France earned its lone point with a doubles win by Benjamin Bonzi and Pierre-Hugues Herbert, who defeated Auger-Aliassime and Duncan Chan, 7-6 (4), 6-3.
Germany 1, Croatia 1
U.S. Open champion Alexander Zverev gave host Germany a 1-0 lead with a 6-4, 7-6 (3) win over Matej Dodig in Halle. Dino Prizmic got Croatia level with a 6-4, 6-3 victory over Daniel Altmaier.
Great Britain 2, Ecuador 0
Great Britain swept the first day in singles in London, as Toby Samuel rallied to beat Andy Andrade 4-6, 6-4, 6-1, and Arthur Fery got past Alvaro Guillen Meza 7-5, 6-0.
Spain 2, Chile 0
Daniel Merida and Rafael Jodar opened with singles victories in Santiago. Merida downed Alejandro Tabilo 5-7, 6-3, 6-3, and Jodar dominated Cristian Garin 6-0, 6-2.

items.author: Reuters

items.summary: Iva Jovic doubled her number of career WTA Tour titles on Saturday in the same event, winning the Guadalajara Open for the second consecutive year.
items.body:
Iva Jovic doubled her number of career WTA Tour titles on Saturday in the same event, winning the Guadalajara Open for the second consecutive year.
The second seed did not drop a set all week, including her 6-4, 6-2 victory over fellow American Peyton Stearns in one hour and 26 minutes in the final of the Mexico tournament.
Jovic, ranked No. 16 in the world, did not face a break point while converting three of five opportunities. The 18-year-old Los Angeles native won 70% of her service points (40 of 57) to 59% (30 of 51) for Stearns.
Stearns, ranked No. 60, also has two career tournament wins on tour: at Rabat, Morocco, in May 2024, and at Austin, Texas, in February 2026.
SP Open
Both higher-seeded players lost in the semifinals at Sao Paulo, with Spain's Kaitlin Quevedo and Argentina's Nadia Podoroska advancing to the finals.
Quevedo, the seventh seed, downed fourth-seeded Anna Blinkova of France 6-4, 2-6, 6-4 in two hours, 23 minutes. Quevedo overcame seven double faults and won 4 of 13 break-point opportunities, to 4 of 8 for Blinkova.
Podoroska, who is unseeded and ranked No. 317 in the world, defeated second-seeded Paula Badosa of Spain 6-3, 6-4 in 1:29. Podoroska won 6 of 11 break-point chances, to 3 of 7 for Badosa, the No. 70-ranked player who had more aces (2-1) and fewer double faults (8-9).
--Field Level Media

items.title: Moscou et sa région visées par des centaines de drones ukrainiens
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Les autorités russes ont annoncé dimanche que Moscou et sa région avaient été la cible durant la nuit de centaines de drones ukrainiens, qui ont fait deux morts, au troisième et dernier jour des élections législatives dans le pays.
items.body:
Les autorités russes ont annoncé dimanche que Moscou et sa région avaient été la cible durant la nuit de centaines de drones ukrainiens, qui ont fait deux morts, au troisième et dernier jour des élections législatives dans le pays.
En Ukraine, quatre personnes dont trois enfants ont été également tuées durant la nuit lors d'attaques russes sur la région de Kyiv, ont rapporté les autorités régionales.
Sur la messagerie Telegram, le maire de Moscou, Sergueï Sobianine, a déclaré que la ville n'avait pas connu pareille offensive depuis le début de l'invasion à grande échelle de l'Ukraine par l'armée russe en février 2022.
La Russie a abattu plus de 1.600 drones depuis samedi, dont 450 visant Moscou, a-t-il dit.
"Cette attaque sans précédent avait été clairement planifiée pour perturber les élections", a-t-il ajouté. "L'adversaire a échoué dans son objectif."
Plusieurs de ces engins sont tombés près d'une raffinerie pétrolière, un autre a touché un appartement, a précisé Sergueï Sobianine, en déclarant qu'aucune victime n'était à déplorer, les deux décès ayant été enregistrés hors de la capitale.
Dans le village de Sofyino, au sud de Moscou, un corps recouvert d'une couverture tachée gisait devant un immeuble résidentiel endommagé, dont les fenêtres des étages supérieurs avaient volé en éclats.
"Des vitres ont volé en éclats, les gens se sont mis à hurler et à crier. Je me suis retourné et les portes d'entrée avaient déjà été soufflées. Il y avait des débris partout", a raconté Vitali, qui n'a pas souhaité donner son nom de famille.
Dans un message sur X, le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky a déclaré qu'une installation clé de l'industrie pétrolière russe et une installation logistique avaient été touchées. "Il s'agit de milliards de dollars qui alimentent la machine de guerre", a-t-il ajouté.
Les frappes ukrainiennes ont mis hors service ces derniers mois une part importante des capacités de raffinage de la Russie, provoquant des pénuries de produits pétroliers, une hausse des prix du carburant et de longues files d'attente dans les stations-service de nombreuses régions.
L'usine de Moscou, qui a été visée à plusieurs reprises, a traité 11,6 millions de tonnes de pétrole en 2024, produisant 2,9 millions de tonnes d'essence et 3,2 millions de tonnes de gazole, selon les dernières données disponibles.
Dans la région de Moscou, outre les deux décès, 400 personnes — dont 70 enfants — ont été évacuées d'un immeuble résidentiel de 21 étages dans le district de Ramenskoïe, et plusieurs habitations ont été endommagées, a indiqué le gouverneur Andreï Vorobiov.
Dans la partie de la région ukrainienne de Kherson occupée par les Russes, une attaque de drone contre un autobus a fait deux morts dont un responsable électoral, a déclaré la présidente de la commission électorale centrale de Russie, Ella Pamfilova.
En Ukraine, une mère et ses deux enfants de 3 ans ont été tués par une frappe de drone sur leur maison, ont rapporté les secours. Une fille est morte à l'hôpital après une autre frappe, a déclaré le gouverneur de l'oblast de Kyiv, Timour Tkatchanko.
Trente et un sites ont été endommagés dans cinq districts, a-t-il dit.

items.body:
The death toll from an overnight Russian attack on the Kyiv region rose to four, including three children, Kyiv regional authorities said on Sunday.
A mother and her two 3-year-old children were killed in Ukraine's Kyiv region when a Russian drone strike hit a private home, the emergency service said.
Kyiv region governor Tymur Tkachanko said a girl died in hospital after a separate drone strike in another district.
Tkachenko said the region endured more than a day of hostile attacks, with 31 sites damaged in five districts.
The southwestern Fastiv district sustained the most damage, with 24 sites hit, including homes, industrial and utility buildings, the grounds of an agricultural enterprise and vehicles, he added.
Russia has been attacking the capital Kyiv and the surrounding Kyiv region with drones continually in recent weeks.

Trump to use Washington triumphal arch as military complex
Reuters | Updated: 20-09-2026 18:55 IST | Created: 20-09-2026 18:55 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump said on Sunday the triumphal arch he plans to build near Arlington National Cemetery in Washington would double as a "military complex" housing drones and snipers, as well as storing large quantities of ammunition.
The president cited national security concerns for the move, echoing the rationale offered for the roughly $400 million ballroom complex being built on the site of the White House's former East Wing, which was demolished to make way for the project. He did not identify any specific threats. The projects are part of Trump's ambitious effort to reshape Washington, including a push to add his name to the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. The plans have drawn criticism from preservationists and others who argue they could alter or diminish historic landmarks.
In a social media post, Trump said that at the "strong request" of the military he had agreed to turn the 250-foot (76-meter) arch "into a top grade Military Complex/Triumphal Arch, to house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large numbers of drones, plus Snipers, on both the roof and plaza areas, and additionally have and hold large quantities of sniper ammunition in storage." The White House and the Department of Defense did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The Federal Aviation Administration said last week that the arch would not pose a hazard to aircraft but would be required to have an "eternal flame" on top, clearing an aviation hurdle for the arch, which Trump proposed to mark the nation's 250th anniversary. Aviation experts have raised safety concerns given its proximity to Reagan Washington National Airport while veterans have sued to block the arch, arguing it would destroy the historic sightline between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

items.title: North Korea fires two ballistic missiles off east coast in three hours
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: North Korea launched two missiles off its eastern coast on Sunday, its second set of tests in roughly a week and days after Pyongyang accused the US of driving tensions on the Korean Peninsula through a series of military drills.
items.body:
North Korea launched two missiles off its eastern coast on Sunday, its second set of tests in roughly a week and days after Pyongyang accused the US of driving tensions on the Korean Peninsula through a series of military drills.
Just three hours after launching a short-range ballistic missile (SRBM) toward the East Sea on Sunday afternoon, North Korea fired another short-range ballistic missile, according to South Korea's defence ministry.
If the subsequent launch is confirmed to be a ballistic missile, it will mark two consecutive ballistic missile tests by North Korea within a three-hour window.
South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said it detected the first test firing from the Wonsan area around 3 p.m. (0600 GMT), identifying the weapon as a ballistic missile. Japan's defence ministry also said it appeared to be a ballistic missile.
Japanese public broadcaster NHK said the projectile had come down outside Japan's exclusive economic zone.
The first projectile flew approximately 450 km (280 miles) and is presumed to belong to the Hwasong-11 series, according to South Korea's military. The second short-range missile, which was also fired from Wonsan at about 5:50 p.m. (0850 GMT), flew more than 600 km (373 miles), it said.
"South Korean and US intelligence authorities have been tracking and sharing related developments from the initial stage of the launch, and have also shared information regarding the 'North Korean ballistic missile' with Japan," the South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff said.
South Korea's National Security Council condemned the short-range missile launch, which follows a test on September 12. The council urged Pyongyang to immediately cease missile activity, warning the test directly violated UN Security Council resolutions.
Japan also lodged a protest through embassy channels in Beijing, according to a Nikkei report.
"This series of North Korean actions threatens the peace and security of Japan, the region, and the international community," Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi was quoted as saying by Nikkei.
On Saturday, North Korea dismissed a resolution by the UN nuclear watchdog against Pyongyang's nuclear programme.
Pyongyang last week also condemned a US-led naval drill which included South Korea and Japan and which ran from August 29 to September 10 near Guam.
North Korea's Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of leader Kim Jong Un, on Friday [USN:L1N45910T TEXT:"blamed"] US-led military drills for "ever-worsening" tensions on the Korean Peninsula and vowed no change in the country's course to strengthen its nuclear arsenal.

items.title: Iran warns against new escalation by US and allies
items.summary: Iran warned on Sunday against any big new attack by the United States and its allies, saying it had information such a move was being prepared, adding to the anxiety in a region already on edge ...
items.body:
Iran warns against new escalation by US and allies
Reuters | Updated: 20-09-2026 18:46 IST | Created: 20-09-2026 18:46 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Iran warned on Sunday against any big new attack by the United States and its allies, saying it had information such a move was being prepared, adding to the anxiety in a region already on edge after drone and missile strikes on Saudi Arabia.
Iran's military central command said on state media that any new attack would trigger sustained retaliation against US bases and interests, and that Washington's regional allies would be considered parties to the conflict. It did not elaborate on the information it said it had about a coming US attack. The US State Department issued a security alert on Saturday saying there was potential for unforeseen escalation in the Middle East and Americans should exercise more vigilance and be aware of possible flight cancellations and airspace closures.
Nearly seven months into the US-Iran war, neither side has looked ready to make major concessions needed to end the fighting and with global energy markets already stretched, the conflict continues to spill over into other crises around the region. On Saturday Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis, who made major advances along Yemen's Red Sea coast after the country's civil war reignited this month, said they had carried out strikes in the Saudi capital Riyadh and on a major oil facility in the kingdom's Red Sea port of Yanbu.
Reuters video showed a massive plume of black smoke billowing from the area of Riyadh's main international airport after booms were heard in the Saudi capital overnight. Saudi Arabia did not comment on the incident or the Houthi claims, though a Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had foiled other attacks on the kingdom. The US State Department alert cited Houthi hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including civilian airports.
Recent escalation by the Houthis has forced Riyadh into a painful dilemma: continue airstrikes on the group to stop it seizing more Yemeni territory or step back in the hopes of averting drone strikes on critical infrastructure. STRIKES ON SAUDI ARABIA
The Houthi gains along the coast mean the group's forces now sit on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, giving them easier control over shipping travelling between the Red Sea and Asia and the ability to blockade the crucial waterway. With Iran already having blockaded most shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, the oil-rich Gulf's energy exports are now almost entirely cut off from global markets, adding to pressure on global oil prices.
A US blockade of Iranian ports is meanwhile stopping Iran from selling its own oil, contributing to major problems in the Islamic Republic's economy. With the war inflicting painful damage on all sides, however, there is little sign of a return to the interim ceasefire agreement that was struck in June but that fell apart in July amid disputes over its terms.
Iran reiterated on Sunday that it would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the terms of that June agreement, as it interpreted them, were met. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said Iran would have to keep on fighting as well as negotiating, to push back its enemies and to consolidate any gains with diplomacy.

items.title: トランプ氏、AI責任者を任命へ－安全上のリスクはでっち上げと一蹴
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： トランプ米大統領は、AI政策を統括する責任者を任命すると表明した。AIの安全性を巡る懸念が高まる中でも、テクノロジー企業に開発を加速するよう促す姿勢を崩していない。

急速に進化するAI技術が人間にリスクをもたらすとの懸念について、トランプ氏はでっち上げだと一蹴。気候変動を巡る警告や、第1次政権時の2度の弾劾訴追につながったスキャンダルになぞらえた。

トランプ氏は19日、SNSへの投稿で「われわれは、この素晴らしい産業の成長をいかなる形でも妨げたり、抑え込んだりすることはない」と強調。「AIは次の産業革命、あるいはインターネットとも言えるが、その規模と影響はさらに大きくなり、わが国の国内総生産（GDP）の最大25%を占める可能性がある」と述べた。

この1週間、米主要AI企業の経営トップらは、技術を巡るリスクが高まっているとして、最先端かつ収益性の高いモデルの開発ペースを落とす必要性を訴えている。

アルファベット傘下のグーグル、OpenAI、アンソロピック、メタ・プラットフォームズはいずれも、自社のAIエージェントが他社のシステムに不正侵入した事例を明らかにしている。

しかし、トランプ氏は開発ペースを落とすことには否定的だ。ウォール街のストラテジストも、AIへの期待が株式相場を大きくけん引してきたと指摘している。

トランプ氏は19日の投稿で、AI産業に関連する問題への対応を支援するため、第1次政権で創設した米軍の一部門である宇宙軍をモデルにAIフォースも創設すると表明した。ただ、その組織形態や具体的な役割は明らかになっていない。

トランプ氏は米国のAI開発について「われわれは中国、そして世界の他の国々をリードしている。私はその状態を維持するつもりだ！」と投稿した。

民主党議員を中心とする多くの議員は、安全性確保に向けて政府がAI技術を規制するよう求める声を強めている。

items.title: Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong's first leader under Chinese rule, laid to rest
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong's first chief executive after the territory's handover from Britain to China, was laid to rest in a state funeral on Sunday.
items.body:
Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong's [USN:L4N3050L2 TEXT:"first chief executive"] after the territory's handover from Britain to China, was laid to rest in a state funeral on Sunday.
Tung, who took office in 1997 as Hong Kong emerged from more than 150 years of British colonial rule, died on September 8 at the age of 89.
Andrew Tung Lieh-cheung, son of the late shipping magnate and heir to the Orient Overseas Container Line empire, carried a portrait of his father at the Hong Kong Funeral Home in the North Point district, where bouquets of white flowers lined the entrance.
Tung's wife Betty Tung Chiu Hung-ping was seen being supported by family members as she left the memorial, according to local media.
Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee was among the pallbearers carrying Tung's casket, which was draped with a Chinese flag.
Shi Taifeng , Politburo member and head of the Communist Party's Organisation Department, which oversees personnel decisions, delivered an eulogy, lauding Tung as an "outstanding contributor to 'one country, two systems'" and a "close friend of the Communist Party of China", Xinhua reported.
Tung's successors Donald Tsang, C.Y. Leung and Carrie Lam also paid their respects.
Elected in 1996 by a Beijing-backed selection committee, Tung became Hong Kong's first chief executive under the "one country, two systems" framework and had to steer the city through the Asian financial crisis that hit in 1997, sparking a recession.
In 2003, Tung tried to push through a security law seen as encroaching on Hong Kong's freedoms, triggering widespread protests. Article 23 was ultimately adopted in 2024 by a pro-Beijing legislature.
Tung was also criticized for the government's response to the SARS epidemic in 2003.
Tung stepped down as chief executive in 2005 and that same year became vice chairman of top advisory body, the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference. He later accompanied Xi Jinping on visits to the U.S. in 2012 and 2015.
Tung founded the nonprofit U.S.-China Exchange Foundation, which promoted people-to-people exchanges and was later criticized for its connections to the Chinese government.
He became an outspoken critic of Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests that flared up in 2019.

items.title: Germany's IW institute triples growth forecast for 2026
items.author: Maria Martinez
items.creator: Maria Martinez
items.summary: Germany's economy is set to grow by nearly 1.2% in 2026, helped by stronger exports and government spending in the first half, according to new forecats by the German Economic Institute (IW) seen by Reuters on Sunday.
items.body:
Germany's economy is set to grow by nearly 1.2% in 2026, helped by stronger exports and government spending in the first half, according to new forecats by the German Economic Institute (IW) seen by Reuters on Sunday.
IW had projected growth of only 0.4% in its previous forecasts published in May.
The economic institutes Ifo, DIW, RWI and [USN:L8N4590G5 TEXT:"IMK have also"] recently raised their forecasts, following a stronger-than-expected first half of the year.
IW warned that momentum would fade in the second half as high energy prices, weak private investment and job losses weigh on demand.
IW forecast slower growth of nearly 1% in 2027, saying consumption and investment would each contribute about half of the expansion.
IW said real exports would rise 2.8% this year and imports 2%, after goods exports rose sharply in the second quarter, partly because of inventory effects.
It cautioned that the boost in exports was likely temporary and structural pressures, including high production costs, protectionism and Chinese competition, remained.
Private consumption is expected to increase only 0.3% in 2026, as inflation of more than 2.5% erodes purchasing power.

items.title: Agenda de la semana: reunión Trump-Xi, tasas en México y minutas de Brasil
items.author: Leidys Becerra
items.summary: México mantendrá el foco de los mercados con su decisión de política monetaria, mientras Brasil actualizará sus perspectivas de inflación y Argentina y Colombia divulgarán nuevos indicadores económico ...
items.body: La reunión entre el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, y el mandatario chino, Xi Jinping, será uno de los principales focos de los mercados esta semana, mientras los inversores siguen de cerca la relación entre las dos mayores economías del mundo y sus implicaciones para el comercio global. Ver más: Reunión Xi-Trump: inversores buscan señales sobre rivalidad en IA y perspectivas del yuan En América Latina, México decidirá su tasa de interés y publicará nuevos datos de inflación y actividad económica, mientras Brasil divulgará las minutas de su reunión de política monetaria y su informe trimestral. En Argentina se conocerá el dato de actividad económica de julio y Colombia publicará su balanza comercial. En Estados Unidos, los mercados seguirán las intervenciones de funcionarios de la Reserva Federal y nuevos datos económicos, mientras en Europa y Asia se conocerán indicadores de actividad, inflación y confianza. En el frente corporativo, Novo Nordisk celebrará su día para inversores y Meta realizará su conferencia Connect, con la inteligencia artificial y sus dispositivos entre los temas centrales. Ver más: Meta apuesta por sus propios chips de IA para reducir costos y consumo de energía Estos son los principales eventos e indicadores económicos de la semana: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo que espera alcanzar varios acuerdos con el mandatario chino, Xi Jinping, durante la visita que el líder asiático realizará a la Casa Blanca la próxima semana. El encuentro llega después de los esfuerzos de ambos gobiernos por reducir las tensiones comerciales y abordar otros puntos de fricción en su relación. La inteligencia artificial será otro de los temas de interés, en medio de la competencia entre ambas potencias por el desarrollo de esta tecnología. Ver más: Bessent se reunirá con su homólogo chino antes de la cumbre entre Trump y Xi Trump ofrecerá el jueves una cena de Estado en honor a Xi, a la que se espera que asistan ejecutivos tecnológicos como Tim Cook, de Apple; Sam Altman, de OpenAI; y Cristiano Amon, de Qualcomm, lo que añade un componente empresarial a la reunión. De acuerdo con un análisis de Bloomberg Economics elaborado por los economistas Felipe Hernández y Adriana Dupita, junto con la analista Jimena Zúñiga , la semana estará marcada por la decisión de tasas de México, las minutas y el informe de política monetaria de Brasil, así como por nuevos datos de actividad e inflación en la región. En Brasil, las minutas de la reunión de septiembre del banco central y su informe trimestral de política monetaria ofrecerán más detalles sobre el rumbo de las tasas. El Banco Central de Brasil justificó el recorte de 25 puntos básicos a 13,75% por el enfriamiento del crecimiento y de la inflación subyacente, además de una postura monetaria todavía restrictiva. Bloomberg Economics espera que el organismo vuelva a recortar la tasa en 25 puntos básicos tanto en noviembre como en diciembre. Ver más: Brasil baja su tasa de interés a 13,75% mientras la inflación y la economía pierden impulso Las minutas podrían ofrecer señales sobre los riesgos para la inflación derivados de los precios del petróleo y El Niño, así como sobre los riesgos para el crecimiento relacionados con el crédito. El informe de política monetaria, por su parte, actualizará la proyección de inflación para el segundo trimestre de 2028 y la estimación de la brecha del producto. El dato de inflación IPCA-15 de mediados de septiembre también estará bajo la lupa. Bloomberg Economics espera un repunte de la inflación frente a mediados de agosto, debido principalmente a la reversión del efecto de un crédito extraordinario en las tarifas eléctricas. También prevé un aumento de las tarifas aéreas, parcialmente compensado por una ligera disminución de los precios de los combustibles. Ver más: Brasil pierde empresas en bolsa ante bajas valoraciones y menor negociación de acciones En México, el banco central probablemente mantendrá su tasa de interés en 6,5% por tercera reunión consecutiva, mientras espera señales más claras de que la inflación mantiene su trayectoria descendente. Aunque el débil crecimiento y la demanda interna respaldan la posibilidad de nuevos recortes, las expectativas de inflación todavía elevadas reducen el margen para bajar las tasas. La inflación quincenal de septiembre también será relevante. Bloomberg Economics estima que habría aumentado a 3,3% interanual en la primera mitad del mes, impulsada principalmente por los precios de los alimentos y efectos de base. La inflación subyacente, en tanto, habría descendido ligeramente a 3,8%. Los datos de ventas minoristas y actividad económica permitirán medir la evolución de la economía. Las ventas minoristas habrían aumentado 2,5% interanual en julio, con un rebote mensual después de las caídas de mayo y junio. La actividad económica, por su parte, habría crecido 3,1% interanual en julio, también con una recuperación mensual. Ver más: Fitch: Presupuesto 2027 deja dudas sobre si México logrará una consolidación que frene la deuda Bloomberg Economics señala que la manufactura, la construcción y los servicios muestran señales de recuperación, aunque el desempeño sigue siendo desigual. La economía continúa operando por debajo de su potencial y los riesgos para el crecimiento están sesgados a la baja. En Argentina, el índice de actividad económica de julio probablemente mostró un crecimiento modesto, si es que lo hubo. Los indicadores adelantados, entre ellos manufactura, construcción e importaciones, mostraron caídas interanuales, mientras que el crecimiento de las exportaciones y la producción minera también se desaceleró. El dato además estará afectado por un efecto calendario negativo, debido a que julio tuvo un día menos que el mismo mes de 2025. Bloomberg Economics considera que la actividad pudo haber retrocedido marginalmente después del sólido avance de junio y señala que la tendencia subyacente parece más débil que hace algunos meses. Ver más: Economía argentina anota primer trimestre de contracción desde 2024 En Colombia, la balanza comercial de julio será el principal dato regional del inicio de la semana. Bloomberg Economics estima que el déficit comercial se amplió a US$2.670 millones, desde US$1.690 millones un año antes. Las exportaciones habrían aumentado a US$4.690 millones, impulsadas principalmente por los mayores precios del petróleo y el oro, además de las ventas de café. Sin embargo, las importaciones habrían crecido con mayor fuerza, hasta US$7.360 millones, debido principalmente a mayores compras de combustibles y otros bienes intermedios. Ver más: Por qué invertir en Colombia puede ser una apuesta por la recuperación de Venezuela Las exportaciones hacia Estados Unidos, principal socio comercial de Colombia, habrían caído 4,7% interanual, mientras que los envíos hacia Venezuela aumentaron 37,1%, aunque desde una base relativamente pequeña. *Con información de Bloomberg Economics y Bloomberg.

items.title: Angels rally in ninth, take down Twins in 11th
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Christian Moore singled in automatic runner Zach Neto with a bases-loaded comebacker off pitcher Taylor Rogers' leg with two outs in the bottom of the 11th inning as the Los Angeles Angels rallied for a 6-5 victory over the Minnesota Twins on Saturday night in Anaheim, Calif.
items.body:
Christian Moore singled in automatic runner Zach Neto with a bases-loaded comebacker off pitcher Taylor Rogers' leg with two outs in the bottom of the 11th inning as the Los Angeles Angels rallied for a 6-5 victory over the Minnesota Twins on Saturday night in Anaheim, Calif.
Moore drilled a first-pitch sweeper that caromed off the leg of Rogers (6-4) and back toward the third base line as Neto sprinted home.
Tayler Saucedo (1-1) struck out two during a scoreless inning of relief for the Angels (60-95), who tied it at 5-5 in the bottom of the ninth on a one-out homer by Vaughn Grissom.
Jose Siri homered and had two hits and two stolen bases, Adam Frazier had a two-run, pinch-hit double and Mike Trout also had two hits and two walks for Los Angeles.
Ryan Kreidler hit a home run, Victor Caratini went 2-for-5 with two RBIs, Walker Jenkins had two hits and a run and Josh Bell and Royce Lewis each had two hits for Minnesota (72-83).
Minnesota took a 2-0 lead in the third. Jenkins led off with a single and scored an out later on a double into the left-center-field gap by Luke Keaschall. Keaschall then stole third base and scored on a groundout by Austin Martin.
The Twins extended the lead to 3-0 an inning later when Brooks Lee doubled into the left field corner and scored on a single by Caratini.
Los Angeles cut the lead to 3-2 in the bottom of the fourth on a two-run homer by Siri.
Kreidler led off the fifth with his eighth home run, a 383-foot drive to left, to make it 4-2 and Caratini added an RBI single in the eighth for a 5-2 lead.
The Angels closed to 5-4 in the bottom of the eighth on Frazier's pinch-hit double.
Los Angeles then forced extra innings in the bottom of the ninth when Grissom belted his 12th home run, a 400-foot drive to right-center, off A.J. Minter.
Los Angeles starter Reid Detmers allowed four runs on six hits in five innings, snapping a streak of seven straight quality starts. He didn't walk a batter and struck out five, becoming the first Angels pitcher since Shohei Ohtani in 2022 to record 200 strikeouts in a season.
Minnesota starter Joe Ryan pitched five innings, giving up two runs on seven hits and one walk with five strikeouts.
--Field Level Media

items.title: América remonta y rescata empate ante Guadalajara en el "clásico nacional" del fútbol mexicano
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: América remontó el sábado dos goles en contra y rescató un empate por 2-2 ante Guadalajara gracias a un doblete del colombiano Miguel Borja en el "clásico nacional" que enfrentó a los dos clubes más populares del fútbol mexicano.
items.body:
América remontó el sábado dos goles en contra y rescató un empate por 2-2 ante Guadalajara gracias a un doblete del colombiano Miguel Borja en el "clásico nacional" que enfrentó a los dos clubes más populares del fútbol mexicano.
Con la igualada, ambos clubes se mantienen en los primeros lugares de la tabla general que lidera Toluca con 19 puntos. Las "Chivas" de Guadalajara ocupan el segundo puesto con 18 unidades, una más de las que registran las "Águilas" del América que marchan en el tercer lugar.
En el partido correspondiente a la novena jornada del torneo Apertura, disputado en el estadio Azteca de Ciudad de México, Guadalajara generó la primera opción de gol a los 20 minutos con un disparo de Bryan González que atajó el portero Rodolfo Cota.
Cinco minutos después, Cota volvió a evitar el gol de Guadalajara al desviar un potente disparo de Roberto Alvarado.
La presión de Guadalajara tuvo resultado a los 31 minutos cuando González definió con un remate de cabeza en el área tras un largo centro enviado por Omar Govea desde el sector derecho.
El equipo dirigido por el argentino Gabriel Milito siguió presionando en busca del segundo gol que encontró en tiempo de reposición de la primera parte por conducto de Ricardo Marín, quien definió en el área chica después de que Cota rechazó un remate de cabeza de Santiago Sandoval.
En la segunda parte, Guadalajara replegó sus líneas para buscar el contragolpe, dejándole toda la iniciativa al América, que descontó a los 71 minutos con una vistosa chilena de Borja, quien acababa de ingresar al partido, tras centro enviado por el uruguayo Brian Rodríguez desde el sector derecho.
Tres minutos después, Borja registró su doblete al definir sin marca frente a la portería tras recibir un pase de Henry Martín, quien eludió a dos adversarios después de controlar un servicio de Rodríguez.
Guadalajara estuvo cerca de meter el tercer gol a los 76 minutos con un remate de Sandoval que pegó en el poste derecho.
En los minutos finales, ambos clubes generaron opciones de gol que no lograron concretar.
En los otros partidos del sábado, Atlético de San Luis ganó por 3-1 a Necaxa con goles del chileno Felipe Mora, Eduardo Aguila y del portero Christopher Andrade, quien mandó el balón a su propia portería cuando le rebotó en la pierna tras un remate. Para Necaxa, en donde debutó el director técnico peruano Juan Reynoso, anotó el argentino Julián Carranza.
Monterrey derrotó por 1-0 a Cruz Azul con gol de César Garza. En tanto, Atlas y Pumas UNAM empataron por 1-1 con tantos del portugués Luis Leite y Ángel Azuaje, respectivamente.
La jornada se completará el domingo cuando Pachuca enfrente a Tijuana, Toluca sea local ante Santos Laguna y León visite a Querétaro.
El viernes, Bravos de Ciudad Juárez logró su primer triunfo en el torneo tras ganar por 2-0 a Tigres UANL con un doblete del colombiano Óscar Estupiñán. En tanto, Puebla y Atlante empataron por 1-1.

items.title: Two dead in Moscow region, drones hit oil refinery in Russian capital
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The largest Ukrainian drone attack reported so far on the Moscow region came as Russia enters the final day of parliamentary elections.
items.body:
The largest Ukrainian drone attack reported so far on Moscow region killed two people and damaged part of an oil refinery in the capital, authorities said on Sunday, as Russia enters the final day of [USN:L6N45B05C TEXT:"parliamentary elections."]
Ukraine and Russia have continued attacks on each other's energy infrastructure despite an [USN:FWN4560K2 TEXT:"announcement"] by US President Donald Trump on Monday that they had agreed to stop.
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said on his Telegram channel that Russia had downed more than 1,600 drones since Saturday, including 450 headed for Moscow.
"The unprecedented attack was clearly planned with the aim of disrupting the elections," he said. "The adversary failed to achieve this."
Several drones reached the premises of the oil refinery and one hit an apartment building, he said.
In the village of Sofyino, south of Moscow, a body covered in a stained blanket lay in front of a damaged apartment block, the upper windows of which were blown out.
"Glass went flying, people started screaming and shouting. I turned around, and the entrance doors had already been blown out, debris everywhere," said resident Vitaliy, who gave only his first name.
A facility at the Moscow refinery was damaged in the attack, Mayor Sobyanin said, without giving further details, news agency Interfax reported.
Reuters witnesses in Moscow heard blasts and saw plumes of smoke billowing from the site of the refinery.
Ukrainian strikes have knocked out a significant part of Russia's oil refining capacity, triggering oil product shortages, fuel price increases and long queues at filling stations in many regions across the country's 11 time zones.
The Moscow plant, which has been targeted multiple times, processed 11.6 million metric tons of oil in 2024, producing 2.9 million tons of gasoline and 3.2 million tons of diesel, the latest available data shows.
Ukraine has not commented on the attacks. Both sides say they do not target civilians.
In the wider Moscow region, in addition to the two deaths, 400 people, including 70 children, were evacuated from a 21-storey apartment block in the Ramenskoye district and a number of homes were damaged, said Governor Andrei Vorobyov.

items.title: World leaders meet at UN amid wars, AI risks, questions over relevance
items.summary: World leaders gather in New York for the UN General Assembly with conflicts in West Asia and Ukraine, artificial intelligence risks and the future of the multilateral body high on the agenda ...
items.body:
Home / World News / World leaders meet at UN amid wars, AI risks, questions over relevance

World leaders meet at UN amid wars, AI risks, questions over relevance World leaders gather in New York for the UN General Assembly with conflicts in West Asia and Ukraine, artificial intelligence risks and the future of the multilateral body high on the agenda

The 15-member UN Security Council may hold high-level meetings on Ukraine, AI and the West Asia, including talks with Arab leaders | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters United Nations 5 min read Last Updated : Sep 20 2026 | 6:10 PM IST

Listen to This Article

World leaders gather in New York this week for the UN General Assembly, bracing for President Donald Trump's return to the rostrum for a second year running, with talks centering on the widening conflicts in the West Asia and Ukraine and the risks of artificial intelligence.
  Nearly 130 heads of state meet with the post-World War Two order under strain and with the UN itself struggling to remain relevant and weathering attacks from Trump, who has slashed America's contributions and withdrawn from dozens of UN bodies.
  Chinese leader Xi Jinping, who last addressed the diplomatic jamboree via video in 2021, will skip New York in favor of one-on-one talks with Trump in Washington on Thursday, fueling debate about the UN's relevance in addressing global crises.
 

  Compounding the crisis of morale and finance are questions about the next leader of the 80-year-old organization: Secretary-General Antonio Guterres completes his term at the end of 2026, with no clear frontrunner in the race to replace him.
  The 15-member UN Security Council may hold high-level meetings on Ukraine, AI and the West Asia, including talks with Arab leaders, diplomats said.
Also Read

UN appoints US official Luke Lindberg as World Food Program chief

Women leadership gap a hurdle in development goals, says UN report

Preparing to leave office, UN chief reflects on a world beset by problems

Russia, China veto US proposal to extend UN monitoring of Iran sanctions

Architects of 9/11 weren't hiding in caves: India flags Pak's terror haven

  More than a year into Trump's second term, "we would no longer say that the UN is in freefall, but we would say that it's stuck in an open-ended crisis," said Richard Gowan of the International Crisis Group.
  "The UN may not be in emergency care like it was last year, but it seems to be trapped in a trauma center for the foreseeable future," Gowan said.

  The US avoided losing its vote at the assembly by paying $725 million in contributions to the regular budget this week, but it still owes the organization more than a billion dollars and makes ongoing demands for cuts and reforms. 
Growing AI risks   The assembly meets shortly after several artificial intelligence industry leaders called for a coordinated slowdown of the development of the technology, warning that it could soon improve on its own and escape human control.
  Guterres has said that AI will be a major topic, adding that countries pushing its frontiers should set up "common guardrails in order to avoid this race to the bottom that could lead one day to a gigantic disaster at the global level."

  The secretary-general has long proposed global governance of AI. In 2023, the UN created an advisory body on the technology, with members including tech executives, government officials and academics.
  The warning has put Guterres at odds with Trump, who dismissed AI risks as a "hoax," saying there is a "sick conspiracy" against it and that China would benefit from the doubt being cast on its development. 
West Asia escalation   The West Asia will again be a focus of discussions, as the US-Israeli war on Iran continues to drive global inflation and destabilize the region. Recent gains by Houthi militants threaten shipping in the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait and could further spike energy prices.

  "It's very difficult to have a military solution for that problem, and the experience of fighting in Yemen demonstrated how complicated it is to have successful interventions," said Guterres, adding that the UN's envoy on Yemen was making a "huge effort" to advance talks.
  Peace talks remain stalled, however, as Iran and the US continue to exchange strikes and Trump threatens a major escalation of the war.
  Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is scheduled to address the assembly on Wednesday.
  Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu - wanted by the International Criminal Court over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza that Israel denies - is to speak on Thursday.

  Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas will for the second year running not be at the gathering in person. The US, a close Israeli ally, again denied him a visa. On Thursday, the General Assembly voted to allow Abbas to appear via video.
  There is likely to be a high-level meeting on the conflict in Sudan on the sidelines, diplomats said, although a diplomatic breakthrough is unlikely. 
Ukraine, food security   Also on the agenda is Russia's more than four-year-old war in Ukraine.
  Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov will address the General Assembly. Zelenskiy will likely seek to shore up Ukraine's position ahead of what is expected to be another tough winter, diplomats said.

  The Security Council has been unable to take action to end the conflict because permanent member Russia holds a veto.
  Trump has at times appeared frustrated that he has been unable to broker an end to the war, a goal he declared a priority when he began his second term in January last year. The US president spoke with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin earlier this month, but it was unclear whether he plans to meet Zelenskiy in New York.
  Guterres highlighted the impact the war was having on civilians but also on food security and energy prices.
  "The effective blockade existing in the Black Sea is creating enormous problems that add to the problems generated by the Middle East crisis, and I think it would be very important to find a way to allow Ukrainian exports and Russian exports of food, fertilizers and energy to take place in a safe way through the Black Sea," he said.

items.title: Allemagne-Elections régionales dans deux Länder
items.author: James Mackenzie
items.creator: James Mackenzie
items.summary: Les électeurs allemands sont appelés aux urnes dimanche à l'occasion de deux élections régionales qui devraient accentuer la pression sur le chancelier Friedrich Merz, dont l'avenir est incertain depuis le triomphe de l'extrême droite lors d'un autre scrutin régional ce mois-ci.
items.body:
Les électeurs allemands sont appelés aux urnes dimanche à l'occasion de deux élections régionales qui devraient accentuer la pression sur le chancelier Friedrich Merz, dont l'avenir est incertain depuis le triomphe de l'extrême droite lors d'un autre scrutin régional ce mois-ci.
Les élections régionales ne suscitent généralement pas beaucoup d'intérêt en dehors de l'Allemagne, mais les scrutins organisés en Mecklembourg-Poméranie-Occidentale, un Land rural de l'ancienne Allemagne de l'Est, et à Berlin, la capitale, interviennent après le triomphe de l'AfD (Alternative pour l'Allemagne) en Saxe-Anhalt le 6 septembre, une victoire qui a provoqué une onde de choc en Europe.
Les sondages indiquent qu'il y a peu de chances que l'AfD réitère son exploit lors de l'un ou l'autre des votes qui se dérouleront dimanche.
Ces deux scrutins devraient toutefois mettre en évidence les progrès considérables que le parti d'extrême droite a réalisés ces dernières années et soulever de nouvelles questions quant à la stratégie dite du "pare-feu", en vertu de laquelle les grands partis refusent de conclure des accords de coalition avec l'AfD.
Pour Friedrich Merz, dont la cote de popularité a chuté jusqu'à 14% selon les derniers sondages, le résultat enregistré au début du mois par l'AfD est le dernier d'une série de revers.
Elu l'année dernière sur la promesse de réformes ambitieuses visant à relancer l'économie allemande en stagnation, le chef des chrétiens-démocrates de la CDU a eu du mal à convaincre des électeurs sceptiques, aggravant le mécontentement suscité par des réformes impopulaires en matière de retraites, de fiscalité et de santé.
La désillusion à l'égard de son gouvernement a pesé sur les campagnes électorales tant en Mecklembourg-Poméranie-Occidentale qu'à Berlin, où les électeurs se sont concentrés sur des enjeux tels que la hausse des coûts de l'énergie et du logement.
La flambée des prix des carburants, particulièrement ressentie dans un Land comme le Mecklembourg-Poméranie-Occidentale où beaucoup dépendent de la voiture pour se déplacer, a poussé le chancelier conservateur à convenir de mesures d'allègement avec ses partenaires de coalition sociaux-démocrates (SPD).
Un sondage a montré vendredi que le SPD regagnait du terrain face à l'Afd dans ce Land, les sociaux-démocrates étant crédités de 37% des voix contre 36% pour le parti d'extrême droite.
A Berlin, un sondage montre que le parti de gauche Die Linke (22%) devance désormais la CDU (20%), menaçant ainsi l'emprise des conservateurs sur la mairie dans une campagne dominée par la question du logement.

items.title: US Treasury's Bessent, China's He to launch talks on AI, trade, critical minerals
items.author: David Lawder, Antoni Slodkowski
items.creator: David Lawder, Antoni Slodkowski
items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng are set to meet on Sunday to try to tee up potential agreements on AI, tariffs and critical minerals for a high-stakes Washington summit this week between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
items.body:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng are set to meet on Sunday to try to tee up potential agreements on AI, tariffs and critical minerals for a high-stakes Washington summit this week between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
The meetings at JP Morgan Chase's (JPM.N) headquarters in Manhattan, which also will include US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, are due to start at about 10:30 a.m. (1430 GMT) and are expected to run all day.
Key topics will be the status of a US-China trade truce that is set to expire on November 10, flows of Chinese rare-earth magnets and critical minerals that US officials say are insufficient and potential guard rails for artificial intelligence after reports of key security breaches involving AI models.
The most likely outcome, analysts say, would be for Washington and Beijing to agree on small steps to show they are continuing to avoid escalating tensions in a delicate trade relationship that has major consequences for the global economy.
"I think there will be some show of deliverables because of the fact that it's a presidential summit coming, but I don't feel like we're on the verge of some sort of breakthrough," said Anna Ashton, a longtime China trade analyst and founder of Ashton Intelligence. "I think status quo is probably both sides' general best expectation."
Many of the issues that He, Bessent and Greer will have to work through for Trump and Xi are holdovers from the two leaders' [USN:L6N41R1CR TEXT:"meeting in Beijing"] in May, including an effort on both sides to cut tariffs on non-strategic goods and Chinese pledges to increase purchases of US agricultural goods by $17 billion a year and to purchase more than 200 Boeing aircraft.
The Bessent-He-Greer meeting follows a pattern set over the past 16 months, in which the three officials met in European and Asian cities to tee up potential agreements for Trump and Xi. These efforts included the November 2025 truce reached in Busan, South Korea, which capped US tariffs imposed during Trump's second term in office at about 20% on Chinese goods after tit-for-tat escalation had brought them to triple-digit levels on both sides.
The US Supreme Court later [USN:L6N3ZH003 TEXT:"struck down"] the Trump tariffs that were invoked under a national emergencies law, including duties related to fentanyl trafficking.
Trump's administration has been rebuilding them under new authorities, including restoring a 12.5% tariff on Chinese goods over forced labor allegations. It is finalizing a separate tariff investigation aimed at curbing excess industrial capacity that it says is rampant in China.
Under that truce, China promised to restore the flow of critical minerals to US and global users. However, a senior US official told reporters on Friday that China's performance on that front "has not been up to par" and would be a topic for discussion ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.
NEW TALKS ON AI The Bessent-He discussions on AI are significant because the US and China are the [USN:L1N45700J TEXT:"two major forces"] driving development of advanced AI tools and the global adoption of the technology. Rare earths play a crucial role in the manufacturing of advanced semiconductor technology powering AI.
Bessent said on Friday he expects the discussions to cover [USN:L6N45A12D TEXT:""both open- and closed-weight models.""] Open-weight models are AI systems with publicly accessible core elements where users can download and fine-tune them for specific tasks.
Chinese open-weight models are becoming more popular with US companies because they can be cheaper than closed-weight AI tools such as those developed by Anthropic, OpenAI and other US companies.
"The United States remains the leader in AI. And we are open to discussions on avoiding shared risks and avoiding bifurcation of our two systems," Bessent said in a statement regarding the China talks.
Bessent has called for the US and China to agree on AI "guard rails" aimed at keeping powerful models out of the hands of malign non-state actors.
TARIFF REDUCTIONS, INVESTMENT The US and China also agreed in May to launch discussions to reduce tariffs for non-strategic goods under a so-called "Board of Trade" mechanism along with a similar forum to deal with specific investment issues.
While the Trump administration has tightened restrictions on US companies investing in some industries in China, Reuters reported on Friday that it is [USN:L1N4570SO TEXT:"working on rules"] that would likely allow US pharmaceutical firms to invest in promising Chinese drugs and strike licensing deals for them.
China's Ministry of Commerce said on Saturday that He would also lead a delegation of Chinese companies to the US that would participate in economic and trade consultations ahead of the summit.
The business delegation, which mirrors a [USN:L1N41T02Q TEXT:"group of US CEOs"] that Trump brought to Beijing in May, was announced as Trump expressed openness to Chinese automakers building US factories. US auto industry groups on Friday [USN:L1N45A0MO TEXT:"urged Trump to maintain an effective ban"] on Chinese vehicle sales in the US on national security grounds.

Chinese leader Xi Jinping, who last addressed the diplomatic jamboree via video in 2021, will skip New York in favor of one-on-one talks with Trump in Washington on Thursday, fueling debate about the UN's relevance in addressing global crises.

The 15-member UN Security Council may hold high-level meetings on Ukraine, AI and the Middle East, including talks with Arab leaders, diplomats said.

"The UN may not be in emergency care like it was last year, but it seems to be trapped in a trauma center for the foreseeable future," Gowan said.
The US avoided losing its vote at the assembly by paying $725 million in contributions to the regular budget this week, but it still owes the organization more than a billion dollars and makes ongoing demands for cuts and reforms.
